title: When distress presses on you
lede: The words the Prophet ﷺ turned to at moments of overwhelming distress.
translit: Lā ilāha illā-llāhu-l-ʿAẓīmu-l-Ḥalīm, lā ilāha illā-llāhu Rabbu-s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ, Rabbu-l-ʿarshi-l-ʿaẓīm.
trans: There is no god but Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Magnificent Throne.
arabic: لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ، رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:The Prophet (ﷺ) used to invoke Allah at the time of distress, saying, "La ilaha illal-lahu Al-`Azim, al- Halim, La ilaha illal-lahu Rabbu-s-samawati wal-ard wa Rabbu-l-arsh il-azim

title: When you feel trapped with no way out
lede: Yūnus ﷺ called on Allah from inside the whale, in darkness upon darkness. He was answered.
translit: Lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu mina-ẓ-ẓālimīn.
trans: There is no god but You. Glory be to You. Truly, I have been among the wrongdoers.
story: Yūnus ﷺ left his people in anger and boarded a ship. When the sea rose, lots were cast and he was thrown overboard, swallowed by a great fish. In the dark of the sea, inside the creature, he made this du'ā, and Allah says: *So We answered him and saved him from distress. And thus do We save the believers.* (21:88)
arabic: لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
english_full: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sa`d narrated from his father, from Sa`d that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:“The supplication of Dhun-Nun (Prophet Yunus) when he supplicated, while in the belly of the whale was: ‘There is none worthy of worship except You, Glory to You, Indeed, I have been of the transgressors. (Lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu minaẓ-ẓālimīn)’ So indeed, no Muslim man supplicates with it for anything, ever, except Allah responds to him.”

title: When worry and sadness sit on your chest
lede: A du'ā the Prophet ﷺ said often, naming worry, grief, weakness and debt one by one.
translit: Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika mina-l-hammi wa-l-ḥazan, wa-l-ʿajzi wa-l-kasal, wa-l-jubni wa-l-bukhl, wa ḍalaʿi-d-dayn, wa ghalabati-r-rijāl.
trans: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ، وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ، وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
english_full: Narrated Anas bin Malik:The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say, "O Allah! I seek refuge with You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from being heavily in debt and from being overpowered by (other) men." (See Hadith No)

title: When you have done all you can
lede: Said by Ibrāhīm ﷺ in the fire, and by the believers when armies gathered against them.
translit: Ḥasbunā-llāhu wa niʿma-l-wakīl.
arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا۟ لَكُمْ فَٱخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَـٰنًا وَقَالُوا۟ حَسْبُنَا ٱللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ ٱلْوَكِيلُ
trans: Those to whom people [i.e., hypocrites] said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allāh, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs."1

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you cannot see the end of it
lede: Revealed to comfort the Prophet ﷺ in his hardest years, with the promise repeated twice.
translit: Fa-inna maʿa-l-ʿusri yusrā. Inna maʿa-l-ʿusri yusrā.
arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
trans: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease [i.e., relief]. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you carry guilt
lede: The Prophet ﷺ called this the master of seeking forgiveness.
translit: Allāhumma anta Rabbī, lā ilāha illā anta, khalaqtanī wa anā ʿabduk, wa anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika ma-staṭaʿt. Aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt, abū'u laka bi-niʿmatika ʿalayya wa abū'u laka bi-dhanbī, fa-ghfir lī, fa-innahu lā yaghfiru-dh-dhunūba illā ant.
trans: O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I hold to Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
arabic: سَيِّدُ الاِسْتِغْفَارِ أَنْ تَقُولَ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَىَّ وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ
english_full: Narrated Shaddad bin Aus:The Prophet (ﷺ) said "The most superior way of asking for forgiveness from Allah is: 'Allahumma anta Rabbi la ilaha illa anta, Khalaqtani wa ana `Abduka, wa ana `ala `ahdika wa wa`dika mastata`tu, A`udhu bika min Sharri ma sana`tu, abu'u Laka bini`matika `alaiya, wa abu'u laka bidhanbi faghfir lee fa innahu la yaghfiru adhdhunuba illa anta." The Prophet (ﷺ) added. "If somebody recites it during the day with firm faith in it, and dies on the same day before the evening, he will be from the people of Paradise; and if somebody recites it at night with firm faith in it, and dies before the morning, he will be from the people of Paradise

title: When you think you have gone too far
lede: Allah addresses those who wronged themselves the most, and calls them 'My servants'.
translit: Yā ʿibādiya-lladhīna asrafū ʿalā anfusihim lā taqnaṭū min raḥmati-llāh…
arabic: ۞ قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
trans: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.1 Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When anger rises in you
lede: The Prophet ﷺ said he knew a word that would take it away, if the man would only say it.
translit: Aʿūdhu bi-llāhi mina-sh-shayṭān.
trans: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan.
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ
english_full: Narrated Sulaiman bin Surad:While I was sitting in the company of the Prophet, two men abused each other and the face of one of them became red with anger, and his jugular veins swelled (i.e. he became furious). On that the Prophet said, "I know a word, the saying of which will cause him to relax, if he does say it. If he says: 'I seek Refuge with Allah from Satan.' then all his anger will go away." Somebody said to him, "The Prophet has said, 'Seek refuge with Allah from Satan."' The angry man said, "Am I mad?

title: When someone has wronged you
lede: The Prophet ﷺ warned: between the supplication of the wronged and Allah there is no barrier.
trans: Beware the supplication of the one who has been wronged, for there is no veil between it and Allah.
note: There are no set words. Say it plainly, in your own language. This hadith is the Prophet's ﷺ assurance that it arrives.
arabic: اتَّقِ دَعْوَةَ الْمَظْلُومِ، فَإِنَّهَا لَيْسَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ اللَّهِ حِجَابٌ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Mu`adh to Yemen and said, "Be afraid, from the curse of the oppressed as there is no screen between his invocation and Allah

title: When you are afraid of someone
lede: What the Prophet ﷺ said when he feared harm from a people.
translit: Allāhumma innā najʿaluka fī nuḥūrihim wa naʿūdhu bika min shurūrihim.
trans: O Allah, we place You before them, and we seek refuge in You from their evil.
dissent: Scholars differ on this chain. Zubair Ali Zai grades it Daif. The majority (3 of 4) authenticate it.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَجْعَلُكَ فِي نُحُورِهِمْ وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شُرُورِهِمْ
english_full: Narrated AbuMusa al-Ash'ari: When the Prophet (ﷺ) feared a (group of) people, he would say: "O Allah, we make Thee our shield against them, and take refuge in Thee from their evils

title: When debt is crushing you
lede: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib taught these words to a man who could not pay, words the Prophet ﷺ taught him.
translit: Allāhumma-kfinī bi-ḥalālika ʿan ḥarāmik, wa aghninī bi-faḍlika ʿamman siwāk.
trans: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me independent by Your grace of everyone besides You.
arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلاَلِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
english_full: Ali [may Allah be pleased with him] narrated:that a Mukatib came to him and said: “Indeed I am not capable of my Kitabah so aid me.” He said: “Should I not teach you words that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me? If you had a debt upon you similar to the mountain of Sir, Allah would fulfill it for you. He said: ‘Say: O Allah, suffice me with Your lawful against Your prohibited, and make me independent of all those besides You (Allāhummakfinī biḥalālika `an ḥarāmika, wa aghninī bi faḍlika `amman siwāka).’”

title: When provision is tight
lede: The Prophet ﷺ taught these words to say at the end of the day.
translit: …iqḍi ʿanna-d-dayna wa aghninā mina-l-faqr.
trans: …Settle our debt for us, and free us from poverty.
arabic: اقْضِ عَنَّا الدَّيْنَ وَأَغْنِنَا مِنَ الْفَقْرِ
english_full: Suhail reported that Abu Salih used to command us (in these words):When any one of you intends to go to sleep, he should lie on the bed on his right side and then say:" O Allah. the Lord of the Heavens and the Lord of the Earth and Lord of the Magnificent Throne, our Lord, and the Lord of evervthina, the Splitter of the grain of corn and the datestone (or fruit kernal), the Revealer of Torah and Injil (Bible) and Criterion (the Holy Qur'an), I seek refuge in Thee from the evil of every- thing Thou art to sieze by the forelock (Thou hast perfect control over it). O Allah, Thou art the First, there is naught before Thee, and Thou art the Last and there is naught after Thee, and Thou art Evident and there is nothing above Thee, and Thou art Innermost and there is nothing beyond Thee. Remove the burden of debt from us and relieve us from want." Abu Salih used to narrate it from Abu Huraira who narrated it from Allah's Apostle (ﷺ)

title: When your body hurts
lede: Taught to ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, who complained of a pain he had felt since becoming Muslim.
translit: Bismillāh (×3), then: Aʿūdhu bi-llāhi wa qudratihi min sharri mā ajidu wa uḥādhir (×7).
trans: Place your hand where the pain is. Say 'In the name of Allah' three times, then seven times: 'I seek refuge in Allah and in His power from the evil of what I feel and fear.'
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُ
english_full: Uthman b. Abu al-'As Al-Thaqafi reported that he made a complaint of pain to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) that he felt in his body at the time he had become Muslim. Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:Place your hand at the place where you feel pain in your body and say Bismillah (in the name of Allah) three times and seven times A'udhu billahi wa qudratihi min sharri ma ajidu wa uhadhiru (I seek refuge with Allah and with His Power from the evil that I find and that I fear)

title: When someone you love is ill
lede: Said seven times at the side of one who is sick.
translit: As'alu-llāha-l-ʿAẓīma Rabba-l-ʿarshi-l-ʿaẓīmi an yashfiyak. (×7)
trans: I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, to cure you.
arabic: أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيمَ رَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَكَ
english_full: Ibn 'Abbas narrated that the Prophet (S.A.W) said:"There is no Muslim worshiper who visits one who is ill - other than at the time of death - and he says seven times: As'alullah Al-'Azeem Rabbal 'Arshil 'Azeem an yashfik ('I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne to cure you') except when he will be cured

title: When you have lost someone
lede: The words of those who, when struck by calamity, are promised blessings and mercy from their Lord.
translit: Innā li-llāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn.
arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَـٰبَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَٰتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُهْتَدُونَ
trans: Who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allāh, and indeed to Him we will return." Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you cannot decide
lede: The Prophet ﷺ taught this for every matter, as he taught sūrahs of the Qur'an.
translit: Allāhumma innī astakhīruka bi-ʿilmik, wa astaqdiruka bi-qudratik, wa as'aluka min faḍlika-l-ʿaẓīm…
trans: O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and Your power by Your might, and I ask You of Your immense grace… (prayed after two rakʿahs, naming your need)
arabic: ُ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلاَ أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلاَ أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلاَّمُ الْغُيُوبِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي ـ أَوْ قَالَ عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ ـ فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي ـ أَوْ قَالَ فِي عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ ـ فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ، ثُمَّ رَضِّنِي بِهِ. وَيُسَمِّي حَاجَتَهُ
english_full: Narrated Jabir:The Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach us the Istikhara for each and every matter as he used to teach us the Suras from the Holy Qur'an. (He used to say), "If anyone of you intends to do something, he should offer a two-rak`at prayer other than the obligatory prayer, and then say: 'Allahumma inni astakhiruka bi'ilmika, wa astaqdiruka biqudratika, wa as'aluka min fadlika-l-'azim, fa innaka taqdiru wala aqdiru, wa ta'lamu wala a'lamu, wa anta'allamu-l-ghuyub. Allahumma in kunta ta'lamu anna hadha-lamra khairun li fi dini wa ma'ashi wa 'aqibati `Amri (or said, fi 'ajili `Amri wa ajilihi) fa-qdurhu li, Wa in kunta ta'lamu anna ha-dha-l-amra sharrun li fi dini wa ma'ashi wa 'aqibati `Amri (or said, fi ajili `Amri wa ajilihi) fasrifhu 'anni was-rifni 'anhu wa aqdur li alkhaira haithu kana, thumma Raddani bihi," Then he should mention his matter (need)

title: When you are studying or sitting an exam
lede: The only thing Allah commands His Messenger ﷺ to ask for more of.
translit: Rabbi zidnī ʿilmā.
arabic: فَتَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا
trans: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign,1 the Truth.2 And, [O Muḥammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you have to speak and you are afraid
lede: Mūsā ﷺ asked for this before standing in front of Pharaoh.
translit: Rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī, wa yassir lī amrī, wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī, yafqahū qawlī.
arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى
trans: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand [i.e., relax] for me my breast [with assurance] And ease for me my task And untie the knot from my tongue That they may understand my speech.

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you long for a family
lede: The prayer of the servants of the Most Merciful.
translit: Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyunin wa-jʿalnā li-l-muttaqīna imāmā.
arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّـٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
trans: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes1 and make us a leader [i.e., example] for the righteous."

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you are hoping for a child
lede: Zakariyyā ﷺ asked for this in old age, and was given Yaḥyā ﷺ.
translit: Rabbi hab lī min ladunka dhurriyyatan ṭayyibah, innaka samīʿu-d-duʿā'.
story: Zakariyyā ﷺ was old and his wife could not bear children. He did not ask quietly out of doubt. He asked because he knew who he was asking. *So the angels called to him while he stood praying in the chamber: Allah gives you good tidings of Yaḥyā.* (3:39)
arabic: هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُۥ ۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
trans: At that, Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you want to protect your children
lede: The Prophet ﷺ used these words for his grandsons Ḥasan and Ḥusayn.
parallel: Also in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3371 with the wording aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmah.
translit: Uʿīdhukumā bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmah, min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, wa min kulli ʿaynin lāmmah.
trans: I seek protection for you both in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and every poisonous creature, and from every envious eye.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: أُعِيذُكُمَا بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لاَمَّةٍ
english_full: Ibn ‘abbas said :The Prophet (May peace be upon him) used to seek refuge in Allah for al-Hasan and al-husain, saying ; I seek refuge for both of you in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every poisonous thing and from the evil eye which influences. He would then say; your father sought refuge in Allah by them for Ismail and Ishaq. Abu Dawud said; this is a proof of the fact that the Quran is not created

title: When you step out the door
lede: Whoever says it is guarded, guided and defended.
translit: Bismillāh, tawakkaltu ʿala-llāh, wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā bi-llāh.
trans: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: إِذَا خَرَجَ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ فَقَالَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ لاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ
english_full: Narrated Anas ibn Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: When a man goes out of his house and says: "In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah; there is no might and no power but in Allah," the following will be said to him at that time: "You are guided, defended and protected." The devils will go far from him and another devil will say: How can you deal with a man who has been guided, defended and protected?

title: When you lie down to sleep
lede: The last words of the Prophet ﷺ before sleeping.
translit: Bismika-llāhumma amūtu wa aḥyā.
trans: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
arabic: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا
english_full: Narrated Hudhaifa:Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to go to bed, he would recite: "Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya (With Your name, O Allah, I die and I live)." And when he woke up from his sleep, he would say: "Al-hamdu lil-lahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana; wa ilaihi an-nushur (All the Praises are for Allah Who has made us alive after He made us die (sleep) and unto Him is the Resurrection

title: When a dream frightens you
lede: The Prophet ﷺ taught exactly what to do, and promised it will not harm you.
trans: If one of you sees a dream he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times, seek refuge in Allah from Satan three times, and turn over onto his other side.
note: The Prophet ﷺ also said not to tell anyone about it, and that it will not harm you.
arabic: إِذَا رَأَى أَحَدُكُمُ الرُّؤْيَا يَكْرَهُهَا فَلْيَبْصُقْ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ ثَلاَثًا وَلْيَسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ ثَلاَثًا وَلْيَتَحَوَّلْ عَنْ جَنْبِهِ الَّذِي كَانَ عَلَيْهِ
english_full: Jabir reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:If anyone sees a dream which he does not like, he should spit on his left side three times, and seek refuge with Allah from the Satan three times, and let him turn over from the side on which he was sleeping

title: When you want to be kept safe
lede: Whoever says it three times in the evening, nothing will harm him until morning.
translit: Bismillāhi-lladhī lā yaḍurru maʿa-smihi shay'un fi-l-arḍi wa lā fi-s-samā', wa huwa-s-Samīʿu-l-ʿAlīm. (×3)
trans: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
arabic: مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ يَقُولُ فِي صَبَاحِ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ وَمَسَاءِ كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لاَ يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الأَرْضِ وَلاَ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ فَيَضُرُّهُ شَيْءٌ
english_full: Aban bin `Uthman said:“I heard `Uthman bin `Affan (ra) saying: ‘The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “There is no worshiper who says, in the morning of every day, and the evening of every night: ‘In the Name of Allah, who with His Name, nothing in the earth or the heavens can cause harm, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing (Bismillāh, alladhi lā yaḍurru ma`a ismihi shai'un fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samā', wa huwas-Samī`ul `Alīm)’ – three times, (except that) nothing shall harm him.” And Aban had been stricken with a type of semi-paralysis, so a man began to look at him, so Aban said to him, “What are you looking at? Indeed the Hadith is as I reported it to you, but I did not say it one day, so Allah brought about His decree upon me.”

title: When your faith feels unsteady
lede: The Prophet ﷺ said this often, and when asked why, said hearts are between two of Allah's fingers.
translit: Yā muqalliba-l-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ʿalā dīnik.
trans: O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.
arabic: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ
english_full: Shahr bin Hawshab said:“I said to Umm Salamah: ‘O Mother of the Believers! What was the supplication that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said most frequently when he was with you?” She said: ‘The supplication he said most frequently was: “O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion (Yā Muqallibal-qulūb, thabbit qalbī `alā dīnik).’” She said: ‘So I said: “O Messenger of Allah, why do you supplicate so frequently: ‘O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.’ He said: ‘O Umm Salamah! Verily, there is no human being except that his heart is between Two Fingers of the Fingers of Allah, so whomsoever He wills He makes steadfast, and whomever He wills He causes to deviate.’”

title: When intrusive thoughts attack your faith
lede: The Companions asked about thoughts too terrible to speak. The Prophet ﷺ called that fear itself a sign of clear faith.
trans: That is clear faith.
note: The Companions came to the Prophet ﷺ saying they found thoughts in themselves too terrible to say aloud. He did not scold them. He told them that being horrified by the thought is itself the proof of belief. A heart that did not believe would not recoil.
arabic: ذَاكَ صَرِيحُ الإِيمَانِ
english_full: It is narrated on the authority of Abu Huraira that some people from amongst the Companions of the Apostle (ﷺ) came to him and said:Verily we perceive in our minds that which every one of us considers it too grave to express. He (the Holy Prophet) said: Do you really perceive it? They said: Yes. Upon this he remarked: That is the faith manifest

title: When something good happens
lede: Allah's own promise about thankfulness.
translit: La'in shakartum la-azīdannakum.
arabic: وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ ۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِى لَشَدِيدٌ
trans: And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'"

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When something you did not want happened
lede: The Prophet ﷺ taught what to say instead of 'if only'.
translit: Qadaru-llāhi wa mā shā'a faʿal.
trans: It is the decree of Allah, and He does what He wills.
arabic: قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ
english_full: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:A strong believer is better and is more lovable to Allah than a weak believer, and there is good in everyone, (but) cherish that which gives you benefit (in the Hereafter) and seek help from Allah and do not lose heart, and if anything (in the form of trouble) comes to you, don't say: If I had not done that, it would not have happened so and so, but say: Allah did that what He had ordained to do and your" if" opens the (gate) for the Satan

title: When you feel you cannot carry it
lede: The closing verse of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and Allah answered every line of it with 'Yes'.
translit: Lā yukallifu-llāhu nafsan illā wusʿahā…
arabic: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ ۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَآ إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ ۖ وَٱعْفُ عَنَّا وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَٱرْحَمْنَآ ۚ أَنتَ مَوْلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ
trans: Allāh does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."1

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you are told to be patient and it is hard
lede: Where to actually find the strength for it.
translit: Yā ayyuha-lladhīna āmanu-staʿīnū bi-ṣ-ṣabri wa-ṣ-ṣalāh, inna-llāha maʿa-ṣ-ṣābirīn.
arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ
trans: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allāh is with the patient.

gradings: Qur'anic text in the Uthmani script via Quran.com; translation: Saheeh International

title: When you wake and the day begins
lede: The Prophet ﷺ taught this to say as the morning comes.
translit: Aṣbaḥnā wa aṣbaḥa-l-mulku lillāh, wa-l-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah.
trans: We have entered the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner.
arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ
english_full: Abdullah reported that when it was evening Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to supplicate:" We have entered upon evening and so, too, the whole Kingdom of Allah has entered upon evening. Praise is due to Allah. There is no god but Allah, the One having no partner with Him." He (the narrator) said: I think that he also uttered (in this supplication these words):" His is tne Sovercignty and to Him is praise due and He is Potent over everything. My Lord, I beg of Thee good that lies in this night and good that follows it and I seek refuge in Thee from the evil that lies in this night and from the evil of that which follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in Thee from sloth, from the evil of vanity. My Lord, I seek refuge in Thee from torment of the Hell-Fire and from torment of the grave." And when it was morning he said like this:" We entered upon morning and the whole Kingdom of Allah enter ed upon morning

title: When the day closes
lede: The same words, turned towards the evening.
translit: Amsaynā wa amsa-l-mulku lillāh, wa-l-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah.
trans: We have entered the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner.
arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ
english_full: Abdullah reported that when it was evening Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to supplicate:" We have entered upon evening and so, too, the whole Kingdom of Allah has entered upon evening. Praise is due to Allah. There is no god but Allah, the One having no partner with Him." He (the narrator) said: I think that he also uttered (in this supplication these words):" His is tne Sovercignty and to Him is praise due and He is Potent over everything. My Lord, I beg of Thee good that lies in this night and good that follows it and I seek refuge in Thee from the evil that lies in this night and from the evil of that which follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in Thee from sloth, from the evil of vanity. My Lord, I seek refuge in Thee from torment of the Hell-Fire and from torment of the grave." And when it was morning he said like this:" We entered upon morning and the whole Kingdom of Allah enter ed upon morning

title: When you set out on a journey
lede: Said by the Prophet ﷺ once he had settled onto his mount.
translit: Subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn.
trans: Glory be to the One who has made this subject to us, when we could never have done it ourselves. And to our Lord we are surely returning.
arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالأَهْلِ
english_full: Ibn Umar (Allah be pleased with them) reported that whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) mounted his camel while setting out on a journey, he glorified Allah (uttered Allah-o-Akbar) thrice, and then said:Hallowed is He Who subdued for us this (ride) and we were not ourselves powerful enough to use It as a ride, and we are going to return to our Lord. O Allah, we seek virtue and piety from Thee in this journey of ours and the act which pleaseth Thee. O Allah, lighten this journey of ours, and make its distance easy for us. O Allah, Thou art (our) companion during the journey, and guardian of (our) family. O Allah, I seek refuge with Thee from hardships of the journey, gloominess of the sights, and finding of evil changes in property and family on return. And he (the Holy Prophet) uttered (these words), and made this addition to them: We are returning, repentant, worshipping our Lord. and praising Him

title: When it rains
lede: Two words the Prophet ﷺ said as the rain came down.
translit: Allāhumma ṣayyiban nāfiʿan.
trans: O Allah, make it a rain that brings good.
arabic: صَيِّبًا نَافِعًا
english_full: Narrated Aisha:Whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saw the rain, he used to say, "O Allah! Let it be a strong fruitful rain

title: When you sit with someone who is ill
lede: What the Prophet ﷺ would say to comfort the one who was sick.
translit: Lā ba's, ṭahūrun in shā' Allāh.
trans: No harm, it is a cleansing, if Allah wills.
note: He said it to comfort, not to minimise. Illness in Islam is spoken of as something that washes a person, not only something that wounds them.
arabic: لاَ بَأْسَ طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:The Prophet (ﷺ) paid a visit to a sick bedouin. The Prophet (ﷺ) when visiting a patient used to say, "No harm will befall you! May Allah cure you! May Allah cure you!" So the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the bedouin. "No harm will befall you. May Allah cure you!" The bedouin said, "You say, may Allah cure me? No, for it is a fever which boils in (the body of) an old man, and will lead him to the grave." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes, then may it be as you say

title: When you want to be kept safe
lede: The greatest verse in the Qur'an. Whoever says it at night has a protector from Allah until morning.
translit: Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa-l-Ḥayyu-l-Qayyūm…
arabic: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
trans: Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living,1 the Self-Sustaining.2 Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them,3 and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursī4 extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High,5 the Most Great.6
