He was asked: At what did you laugh? He replied: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do as I have done, and laugh after that. I asked: Messenger of Allah , at what are you laughing? He replied: Your Lord, Most High, is pleased with His servant when he says: "Forgive me my sins." He know that no one forgives sins except Him

title: What he said when they asked him to fix prices
lede: Prices had risen and the people came with a reasonable request.
translit: Inna-Llāha huwa-l-musaʿʿiru-l-qābiḍu-l-bāsiṭu-r-rāziq
trans: Allah is the One who sets the price, who withholds, who gives abundantly, who provides.
story: The cost of living rose in Madinah and they asked him to fix prices by decree. He refused, and gave the reason: he hoped to meet his Lord with no one holding a claim against him over blood or wealth. Four names of Allah in a row, two of them opposites, sitting inside a conversation about the market.
arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمُسَعِّرُ الْقَابِضُ الْبَاسِطُ الرَّازِقُ
english_full: It was nanated that Anas bin Malik said:"Prices rose during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, prices have risen, so fix the prices for us.' He said: 'Indeed Allah is the Musa'ir, [1] the Qabid, (Restrainer) the Basit,[2] the Razzaq (Provider). And I am hopeful that I meet my Lord and none of you are seeking (recompense from) me for an injustice involving blood or wealth

title: What he said as the body went down
lede: Six words, said at the edge of the grave.
translit: Bismi-Llāhi wa ʿalā sunnati rasūli-Llāh
trans: In the name of Allah, and upon the way of the Messenger of Allah.
story: Ibn ʿUmar reports it as what he said at the moment the body was placed in. Nothing about the person, nothing about the loss. Just the name it began under and the road it was walked on.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَعَلَى سُنَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ
english_full: Narrated Abdullah ibn Umar: When the Prophet (ﷺ) placed the dead in the grave, he said: In the name of Allah, and following the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is Muslim's version

title: What he said standing over a sick person
lede: He asked for the kind of cure that does not leave a trace behind.
translit: Adhhibi-l-baʾsa rabba-n-nās, ishfi wa anta-sh-shāfī, lā shifāʾa illā shifāʾuk, shifāʾan lā yughādiru saqamā
trans: Take away the harm, Lord of people. Heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing. A healing that leaves no illness behind.
story: Aisha says this is what he did whenever he visited someone ill, or someone ill was brought to him. The last clause is the one people miss. Not just recovery. Recovery that does not leave anything sitting underneath it.
arabic: أَذْهِبِ الْبَاسَ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، اشْفِ وَأَنْتَ الشَّافِي لاَ شِفَاءَ إِلاَّ شِفَاؤُكَ، شِفَاءً لاَ يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
english_full: Narrated `Aisha:Whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) paid a visit to a patient, or a patient was brought to him, he used to invoke Allah, saying, "Take away the disease, O the Lord of the people! Cure him as You are the One Who cures. There is no cure but Yours, a cure that leaves no disease

title: What to say when you stop somewhere
lede: A woman reported it, and a man stung by a scorpion proved it.
translit: Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-Llāhi-t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq
trans: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
story: Khawlah bint Hakim reported it: when one of you stops at a place, say this, and nothing will harm him until he moves on. In the same chapter a man came saying a scorpion had stung him in the night, and was told that had he said it, it would not have hurt him.
note: Said on arriving anywhere you did not choose. A hotel, a hospital, a roadside.
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
english_full: Khaula bint Hakim Sulamiyya reported:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: When any one of you stays at a place, he should say:" I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of that He created." Nothing would then do him any harm until he moves from that place. Abu Huraira reported that a person came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said:" Allah's Messenger, I was stung by a scorpion during the night. Thereupon he said: Had you recited these words in the evening:" I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of what He created," it would not have done any harm to you

title: What He says in the last part of the night
lede: Three questions, repeated until the sky lightens.
translit: Hal min sāʾilin yuʿṭā, hal min dāʿin yustajābu lah, hal min mustaghfirin yughfaru lah, ḥattā yanfajira-ṣ-ṣubḥ
trans: Is there anyone asking, so he may be given? Anyone calling, so he may be answered? Anyone seeking forgiveness, so he may be forgiven? Until dawn breaks.
story: Half the night gone, or two thirds. The questions are not rhetorical and they are not asked once. They are asked over and over into an empty hour, and they stop only when the sun comes up.
arabic: هَلْ مِنْ سَائِلٍ يُعْطَى هَلْ مِنْ دَاعٍ يُسْتَجَابُ لَهُ هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ يُغْفَرُ لَهُ حَتَّى يَنْفَجِرَ الصُّبْحُ
english_full: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:When half of the night or two-third of it is over. Allah, the Blessed and the Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven and says: Is there any beggar, so that he be given? Is there any supplicator so that he be answered? Is there any beggar of forgiveness so that he be forgiven? (And Allah continues it saying) till it is daybreak

title: What the angel keeps saying over an unborn child
lede: Three announcements, then four questions, then it is written.
translit: Yā rabbi nuṭfah, yā rabbi ʿalaqah, yā rabbi muḍghah
trans: My Lord, a drop. My Lord, a clot. My Lord, a morsel of flesh.
story: An angel is assigned to every womb and reports each stage aloud. When Allah wills to complete the creation the angel asks: male or female, wretched or blessed, what provision, what lifespan. And it is written while the child is still inside its mother.
arabic: يَا رَبِّ نُطْفَةٌ، يَا رَبِّ عَلَقَةٌ، يَا رَبِّ مُضْغَةٌ
english_full: Narrated Anas bin Malik:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "At every womb Allah appoints an angel who says, 'O Lord! A drop of semen, O Lord! A clot. O Lord! A little lump of flesh." Then if Allah wishes (to complete) its creation, the angel asks, (O Lord!) Will it be a male or female, a wretched or a blessed, and how much will his provision be? And what will his age be?' So all that is written while the child is still in the mother's womb

title: Why the heat and the cold get that extreme
lede: The Fire complained about something, and was given permission.
translit: Ishtakati-n-nāru ilā rabbihā, fa-qālat rabbi akala baʿḍī baʿḍā, fa-adhina lahā bi-nafasayn: nafasin fi-sh-shitāʾi wa nafasin fi-ṣ-ṣayf
trans: The Fire complained to its Lord and said: my Lord, parts of me are consuming other parts. So He permitted it two breaths, one in winter and one in summer.
story: The worst heat you have ever stood in and the worst cold you have ever been caught in are described here as one exhalation each. Not the thing itself. Its breath.
arabic: اشْتَكَتِ النَّارُ إِلَى رَبِّهَا، فَقَالَتْ رَبِّ أَكَلَ بَعْضِي بَعْضًا، فَأَذِنَ لَهَا بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "The (Hell) Fire complained to its Lord saying, 'O my Lord! My different parts eat up each other.' So, He allowed it to take two breaths, one in the winter and the other in summer, and this is the reason for the severe heat and the bitter cold you find (in weather)

title: Noah is asked who will speak for him
lede: His own nation says nobody ever warned them.
translit: Fa-yaqūlu man yashhadu lak, fa-yaqūlu Muḥammadun wa ummatuh
trans: He will say: who will bear witness for you? He will say: Muhammad and his community.
story: Noah preached for centuries and on that Day his people will say no warner ever came. He is asked who can testify. He names a community that had not yet been born when he was alive. The verse cited is the one about being made a middle nation, witnesses over mankind.
arabic: فَيَقُولُ مَنْ يَشْهَدُ لَكَ فَيَقُولُ مُحَمَّدٌ وَأُمَّتُهُ
english_full: Narrated Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Noah will be called on the Day of Resurrection and he will say, 'Labbaik and Sa`daik, O my Lord!' Allah will say, 'Did you convey the Message?' Noah will say, 'Yes.' His nation will then be asked, 'Did he convey the Message to you?' They will say, 'No Warner came to us.' Then Allah will say (to Noah), 'Who will bear witness in your favor?' He will say, 'Muhammad and his followers. So they (i.e. Muslims) will testify that he conveyed the Message. And the Apostle (Muhammad) will be a witness over yourselves, and that is what is meant by the Statement of Allah "Thus We have made of you a just and the best nation that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Apostle (Muhammad) will be a witness over yourselves

title: The man who could not memorise anything
lede: He was given five phrases, then asked the honest follow-up.
translit: Allāhumma-rḥamnī wa-rzuqnī wa ʿāfinī wa-hdinī
trans: O Allah, have mercy on me, provide for me, keep me well, and guide me.
story: He said: I cannot take anything from the Qurʾān, teach me what will do instead. He was given subḥānallāh, alḥamdulillāh, lā ilāha illā-llāh, allāhu akbar, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh. Then he said: Messenger of Allah, that is all for Allah. What is there for me. And he was given this.
note: Nobody corrected him for asking.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Hasan

arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ ارْحَمْنِي وَارْزُقْنِي وَعَافِنِي وَاهْدِنِي
english_full: Narrated Abdullah ibn AbuAwfa: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: I cannot memorise anything from the Qur'an: so teach me something which is sufficient for me. He said: Say Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is most great, and there is no might and no strength but in Allah. :He said: Messenger of Allah, this is for Allah, but what is for me? He said: Say: O Allah have mercy on me, and sustain me, and keep me well, and guide me. When he stood up, he made a sign with his hand (indicating that he had earned a lot). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: He filed up his hand with virtues

title: What Abu Bakr asked to be given
lede: He wanted something fixed to say at both ends of the day.
translit: Allāhumma fāṭira-s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ, ʿālima-l-ghaybi wa-sh-shahādah, rabba kulli shayʾin wa malīkah, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā ant, aʿūdhu bika min sharri nafsī wa sharri-sh-shayṭāni wa shirkih
trans: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord of everything and its Owner. I testify there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of myself and from the evil of Satan and his idolatry.
story: Abu Bakr asked for words to say morning and evening. He was given these, and then told to say them at a third time as well, when he lay down. The first thing refuge is sought from is not Satan. It is himself.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ رَبَّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِي وَشَرِّ الشَّيْطَانِ وَشِرْكِهِ
english_full: Narrated AbuHurayrah: AbuBakr as-Siddiq said: Messenger of Allah! command me something to say in the morning and in the evening. He said: Say "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Who knowest the unseen and the seen, Lord and Possessor of everything. I testify that there is no god but Thee; I seek refuge in Thee from the evil within myself, from the evil of the devil, and his (incitement to) attributing partners (to Allah)." He said: Say this in the morning

title: A prayer for whoever leads and whoever calls
lede: Both roles are named, with a different word for each.
translit: Al-imāmu ḍāminun wa-l-muʾadhdhinu muʾtaman. Allāhumma arshidi-l-aʾimmata wa-ghfir li-l-muʾadhdhinīn
trans: The imam carries a responsibility and the caller holds a trust. O Allah, guide the imams and forgive the callers.
story: Two jobs, two liabilities. The one in front is answerable for the prayer behind him, so the prayer for him is guidance. The one on the minaret is trusted with the time, so the prayer for him is forgiveness.
arabic: الإِمَامُ ضَامِنٌ وَالْمُؤَذِّنُ مُؤْتَمَنٌ اللَّهُمَّ أَرْشِدِ الأَئِمَّةَ وَاغْفِرْ لِلْمُؤَذِّنِينَ
english_full: Narrated AbuHurayrah: The imam is responsible and the mu'adhdhin is trusted, O Allah, guide the imams and forgive the mu'adhdhins

title: The man who ran, then turned around
lede: Everyone around him had already fled.
translit: Unẓurū ilā ʿabdī rajaʿa raghbatan fīmā ʿindī wa shafaqatan mimmā ʿindī
trans: Look at My servant. He went back, wanting what is with Me and fearing what is with Me.
story: His companions broke and ran. He ran with them. Then he understood what running meant, and he turned around and went back alone, and his blood was spilled. Allah says to the angels: look at him. The praise is not for never having run. It is for the turn.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Hasan

arabic: انْظُرُوا إِلَى عَبْدِي رَجَعَ رَغْبَةً فِيمَا عِنْدِي وَشَفَقَةً مِمَّا عِنْدِي
english_full: Narrated Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Our Lord Most High is pleased with a man who fights in the path of Allah, the Exalted; then his companions fled away (i.e. retreated). But he knew that it was a sin (to flee away from the battlefield), so he returned, and his blood was shed. Thereupon Allah, the Exalted, says to His angels: Look at My servant; he returned seeking what I have for him (i.e. the reward), and fearing (the punishment) I have, until his blood was shed

title: Show mercy down here and it comes from above
lede: The rule is stated twice, once as a name and once as an instruction.
translit: Ar-rāḥimūna yarḥamuhumu-r-Raḥmān. Irḥamū ahla-l-arḍi yarḥamkum man fi-s-samāʾ
trans: The merciful are shown mercy by the Merciful. Have mercy on those on earth and the One above will have mercy on you.
story: Ahl al-arḍ is everyone on the ground. It is not narrowed to believers, or to people you like, or to people. Whatever mercy you want coming down is described here as being paid out first, sideways.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ ارْحَمُوا أَهْلَ الأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ
english_full: Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: The Compassionate One has mercy on those who are merciful. If you show mercy to those who are on the earth, He Who is in the heaven will show mercy to you. Musaddad did not say: The client of 'Adb Allah b. 'Amr. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said

title: What he said bowing, and how long he stayed there
lede: Hudhayfah timed it against the standing.
translit: Subḥāna rabbiya-l-ʿaẓīm
trans: Glory to my Lord, the Mighty.
story: Hudhayfah watched him pray at night. Allāhu akbar three times, then the whole of al-Baqarah, then a bowing about as long as the standing had been, saying this. Then a rising about as long as the bowing. Nothing in it was hurried.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ
english_full: Narrated Hudhayfah: Hudhayfah saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying at night. He said: Allah is most great" three times, "Possessor of kingdom, grandeur, greatness and majesty." He then began (his prayer) and recited Surah al-Baqarah; then he bowed and he paused in bowing as long as he stood up; he said while bowing, "Glory be to my mighty Lord," "Glory be to my mighty Lord" ; then he raised his head, after bowing: then he stood up and he paused as long as he paused in bowing and said, "Praise be to my Lord" ; then he prostrated and paused in prostration as long as he paused in the standing position; he said while prostrating: "Glory be to my most high Lord"; then he raised his head after prostration, and sat as long as he prostrated, and said while sitting: "O my Lord forgive me." He offered four rak'ahs of prayer and recited in them Surah al-Baqarah, Aal Imran, an-Nisa, al-Ma'idah, or al-An'am. The narrator Shu'bah doubted

title: What he said three times at the end of the sermon
lede: He raised his finger to the sky and pointed it back at them.
translit: Allāhumma-shhad, Allāhumma-shhad, Allāhumma-shhad
trans: O Allah, bear witness. O Allah, bear witness. O Allah, bear witness.
story: Jabir describes the farewell pilgrimage in full, and this is how the sermon ends. He asked the crowd whether he had delivered it. They said yes. So he lifted his finger and turned it towards them and called Allah as the witness that he had.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اشْهَدِ اللَّهُمَّ اشْهَدِ اللَّهُمَّ اشْهَدْ
english_full: Ja’far bin Muhammad reported on the authority of his father “We entered upon Jabir bin ‘Abd Allaah. When we reached him, he asked about the people (who had come to visit him). When my turn came I said “I am Muhammad bin Ali bin Hussain. He patted my head with his hand and undid my upper then lower buttons. He then placed his hand between my nipples and in those days I was a young boy.” He then said “welcome to you my nephew, ask what you like. I questioned him he was blind. The time of prayer came and he stood wrapped in a mantle. Whenever he placed it on his shoulders its ends fell due to its shortness. He led us in prayer while his mantle was placed on a rack by his side. I said “tell me about the Hajj of the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ).”He signed with his hand and folded his fingers indicating nine. He then said Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) remained nine years (at Madeenah ) during which he did not perform Hajj, then made a public announcement in the tenth year to the effect that the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) was about to (go to) perform Hajj. A large number of people came to Madeenah everyone desiring to follow him and act like him. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) went out and we too went out with him till we reached Dhu Al Hulaifah. Asma’ daughter of ‘Umais gave birth to Muhammad bin Abi Bakr. She sent message to Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) asking him What should I do?He replied “take a bath, bandage your private parts with a cloth and put on ihram.” The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) then prayed (in the masjid) and mounted Al Qaswa’ and his she Camel stood erect with him on its back. Jabir said “I saw (a large number of) people on mounts and on foot in front of him and a similar number on his right side and a similar number on his left side and a similar number behind him. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) was among us, the Qur’an was being revealed to him and he knew its interpretation. Whatever he did, we did it. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) then raised his voice declaring Allaah’s unity and saying “Labbaik ( I am at thy service), O Allaah, labbaik, labbaik, Thou hast no partner praise and grace are Thine and the Dominion. Thou hast no partner. The people too raised their voices in talbiyah which they used to utter. But the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) did not forbid them anything. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) continued his talbiyah. Jabir said “We did not express our intention of performing anything but Hajj, being unaware of ‘Umrah (at that season), but when we came with him to the House (the Ka’bah), he touched the corner (and made seven circuits) walking quickly with pride in three of them and walking ordinarily in four. Then going forward to the station of Abraham he recited “And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer.” (While praying two rak’ahs) he kept the station between him and the House. The narrator said My father said that Ibn Nufail and ‘Uthman said I do not know that he (Jabir) narrated it from anyone except the Prophet (ﷺ). The narrator Sulaiman said I do not know but he (Jabir) said “The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) used to recite in the two rak’ahs “Say, He is Allaah, one” and “Say O infidels”. He then returned to the House (the ka’bah) and touched the corner after which he went out by the gate to Al Safa’. When he reached near Al Safa’ he recited “Al Safa’ and Al Marwah are among the indications of Allaah” and he added “We begin with what Allaah began with”. He then began with Al Safa’ and mounting it till he could see the House (the Ka’bah) he declared the greatness of Allaah and proclaimed his Unity. He then said “there is no god but Allaah alone, Who alone has fulfilled His promise, helped His servant and routed the confederates. He then made supplication in the course of that saying such words three times. He then descended and walked towards Al Marwah and when his feet came down into the bottom of the valley, he ran, and when he began to ascend he walked till he reached Al Marwah. He did at al Marwah as he had done at Al Safa’ and when he came to Al Marwah for the last time, he said “If I had known before what I have come to know afterwards regarding this matter of mine, I would not have brought sacrificial animals but made it an ‘Umrah, so if any of you has no sacrificial animals, he may take off ihram and treat it as an ‘Umrah. All the people then took off ihram and clipped their hair except the Prophet (ﷺ) and those who had brought sacrificial animals. Suraqah (bin Malik) bin Ju’sham then got up and asked Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ)does this apply to the present year or does it apply for ever? The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) interwined his fingers and said “The ‘Umarh has been incorporated in Hajj. Adding ‘No’, but forever and ever. ‘Ali came from Yemen with the sacrificial animals of the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) and found Fathima among one of those who had taken off their ihram. She said put on colored clothes and stained her eyes with collyrium. ‘Ali disliked (this action of her) and asked Who commanded you for this? She said “My father”. Jabir said ‘Ali said at Iraq I went to Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) to complain against Fathima for what she had done and to ask the opinion of Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) about which she mentioned to me. I informed him that I disliked her action and that thereupon she said to me “My father commanded me to do this.” He said “She spoke the truth, she spoke the truth.” What did you say when you put on ihram for Hajj? I said O Allaah, I put on ihram for the same purpose for which Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) has put it on. He said I have sacrificial animals with me, so do not take off ihram. He (Jabir) said “The total of those sacrificial animals brought by ‘Ali from Yemen and of those brought by the Prophet (ﷺ) from Madeenah was one hundred.” Then all the people except the Prophet (ﷺ) and those who had with them the sacrificial animals took off ihram and clipped their hair. When the 8th of Dhu Al Hijjah (Yaum Al Tarwiyah) came, they went towards Mina having pit on ihram for Hajj and the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) rode and prayed at Mina the noon, afternoon, sunset, night and dawn prayers. After that he waited a little till the sun rose and gave orders for a tent of hair to be set up at Namrah. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) then sent out and the Quraish did not doubt that he would halt at Al Mash ‘ar Al Haram at Al Muzdalifah, as the Quraish used to do in the pre Islamic period but he passed on till he came to ‘Arafah and found that the tent had been setup at Namrah. There he dismounted and when the sun had passed the meridian he ordered Al Qaswa’ to be brought and when it was saddled for him, he went down to the bottom of the valley and addressed the people saying “Your lives and your property must be respected by one another like the sacredness of this day of yours in the month of yours in this town of yours. Lo! Everything pertaining to the pre Islamic period has been put under my feet and claims for blood vengeance belonging to the pre Islamic period have been abolished. The first of those murdered among us whose blood vengeance I permit is the blood vengeance of ours (according to the version of the narrator ‘Uthman, the blood vengeance of the son of Rabi’ah and according to the version of the narrator Sulaiman the blood vengeance of the son of Rabi’ah bin Al Harith bin ‘Abd Al Muttalib). Some (scholars) said “he was suckled among Banu Sa’d(i.e., he was brought up among Bani Sa’d) and then killed by Hudhail. The usury of the pre Islamic period is abolished and the first of usury I abolish is our usury, the usury of ‘Abbas bin ‘Abd Al Muttalib for it is all abolished. Fear Allaah regarding women for you have got them under Allah’s security and have the right to intercourse with them by Allaah’s word. It is a duty from you on them not to allow anyone whom you dislike to lie on your beds but if they do beat them, but not severely. You are responsible for providing them with food and clothing in a fitting manner. I have left among you something by which if you hold to it you will never again go astray, that is Allaah’s Book. You will be asked about me, so what will you say? They replied “We testify that you have conveyed and fulfilled the message and given counsel. Then raising his forefinger towards the sky and pointing it at the people, he said “O Allaah! Be witness, O Allaah! Be witness, O Allaah! Be witness! Bilal then uttered the call to prayer and the iqamah and he prayed the noon prayer, he then uttered the iqamah and he prayed the afternoon prayer, engaging in no prayer between the two. He then mounted (his she Camel) al Qaswa’ and came to the place of standing , making his she Camel Al Qaswa‘ turn its back to the rocks and having the path taken by those who went on foot in front of him and he faced the qiblah. He remained standing till sunset when the yellow light had somewhat gone and the disc of the sun had disappeared. He took Usamah up behind him and picked the reins of Al Qaswa’ severely so much so that its head was touching the front part of the saddle. Pointing with is right hand he was saying “Calmness, O People! Calmness, O people. Whenever he came over a mound (of sand) he let loose its reins a little so that it could ascend. He then came to Al Muzdalifah where he combined the sunset and night prayers, with one adhan and two iqamahs. The narrator ‘Uthamn said He did not offer supererogatory prayers between them. The narrators are then agreed upon the version He then lay down till dawn and prayed the dawn prayer when the morning light was clear. The narrator Sulaiman said with one adhan and one iqamah. The narrators are then agreed upon the version He then mounted Al Qaswa’ and came to Al Mash’ar Al Haram and ascended it. The narrators ‘Uthaman and Sulaiman said He faced the qiblah praised Allaah, declared His greatness, His uniqueness. ‘Uthamn added in his version and His Unity and kept standing till the day was very clear. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) then went quickly before the sun rose , taking Al Fadl bin ‘Abbas behind him. He was a man having beautiful hair, white and handsome color. When the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) went quickly, the women in the howdas also began to pass him quickly. Al Fadl began to look at them. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) placed his hand on the face of Al Fadl , but Al fadl turned his face towards the other side. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) also turned away his hand to the other side. Al Fadl also turned his face to the other side looking at them till he came to (the Valley of) Muhassir. He urged the Camel a little and following a middle road which comes out at the greatest jamrah, he came to the jamrah which is beside the tree and he threw seven small pebbles at this (jamrah) saying “Allah is most great” each time he threw a pebble like bean seeds. He threw them from the bottom of the valley. The Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) then went to the place of the sacrifice and sacrificed sixty three Camels with his own hand. He then commanded ‘Ali who sacrificed the remainder and he shared him and his sacrificial animals. After that he ordered that a piece of flesh from each Camel should be put in a pot and when it was cooked the two of them ate some of it and drank some of its broth. The narrator Sulaiman said the he mounted afterwards the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) went quickly to the House (the Ka’bah) and prayed the noon prayer at Makkah. He came to Banu ‘Abd Al Muttalib who were supplying water at Zamzam and said draw water Banu ‘Abd Al Muttalib were it not that people would take from you the right to draw water, I would draw it along with you. So they handed him a bucket and he drank from it

title: The one condition on the prayer
lede: Short enough to be missed.
translit: Lā tuqbalu ṣalātu aḥadikum idhā aḥdatha ḥattā yatawaḍḍaʾ
trans: The prayer of any of you is not accepted once he breaks his state of purity, until he performs ablution.
story: Not invalid, not incomplete. Not accepted. It is one of the few places where a condition is put on the prayer in that word, and the fix given for it takes two minutes.
arabic: لاَ تُقْبَلُ صَلاَةُ أَحَدِكُمْ إِذَا أَحْدَثَ حَتَّى يَتَوَضَّأَ
english_full: Hammam b. Munabbih who is the brother of Wahb b. Munabbih said:This is what has been transmitted to us by Abu Huraira from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and then narrated a hadith out of them and observed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The prayer of none amongst you would be accepted in a state of impurity until he performs ablution

title: The last man out of the Fire, counting
lede: They were told to ask about his small sins and hide the large ones.
translit: Fa-yaqūlu yā rabbi laqad ʿamiltu ashyāʾa mā arāhā hāhunā
trans: He will say: my Lord, I did things I do not see here.
story: His small sins are read out to him one by one while the large ones are kept back. Then he is told that for every bad deed he has a good one in its place. And he looks at the list and objects, because the worst things he ever did are missing from it. Abu Dharr said he saw the Prophet laugh until his back teeth showed.
note: He is arguing for his own prosecution and losing.
arabic: فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ لَقَدْ عَمِلْتُ أَشْيَاءَ مَا أَرَاهَا هَا هُنَا
english_full: Abu Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w) said:" I know the last of the people of the Fire to depart from the Fire and the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise. A man will be brought forth and He (s.a.w) will say: 'Ask about his small sins and hide his large sins.' So it will be said to him: 'Did you do this and that on such and such a day, did you do this and that on such- and – such a day?'” He said: “Then it will be said to him; 'For each of your sins you shall have a reward.'” He (s.a.w) said: “So he will say: 'O Lord! I have done things that I do not see here.'” He (Abu Dharr) said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w) laugh until his molars were visible.” (Sahih)

title: What the murdered person carries on that Day
lede: Ibn Abbas was asked about repentance afterwards, and read a verse instead of answering.
translit: Yaqūlu yā rabbi hādhā qatalanī, ḥattā yudniyahu mina-l-ʿarsh
trans: He will say: my Lord, this one killed me. Until he brings him right up to the Throne.
story: The one who was killed arrives holding the one who killed him, his own head in his hand, his veins still running. He does not stop at the edge. He walks the man all the way to the Throne. When people raised repentance with Ibn Abbas he recited the verse about killing a believer deliberately and said it was never abrogated.
arabic: يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ هَذَا قَتَلَنِي حَتَّى يُدْنِيَهُ مِنَ الْعَرْشِ
english_full: Narrated 'Amr bin Dinar:from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Judgement, the murdered will come with the murderer's scalp and his head in his hand, and his jugular vein flowing blood saying: 'O Lord! This one killed me!' Until he comes close to the Throne." So they mentioned repentance to Ibn 'Abbas, and he recited this Ayah: And whoever kills a believer intentionally then his recompense is Hell (4:93). He said: "This Ayah was not abrogated nor (its ruling) replaced so from where is his repentance?

title: What he said walking in, and what changed on the way out
lede: One word is different between the two.
translit: Rabbi-ghfir lī dhunūbī wa-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik
trans: My Lord, forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy.
story: Fatimah reports both halves. Going in he sent peace on the Prophet and asked for the doors of mercy. Coming out he sent peace again and asked for the doors of bounty. Mercy is what you go in for. Provision is what you go back out into.
note: On leaving, say faḍlik in place of raḥmatik.
dissent: Scholars differ on this chain. Zubair Ali Zai grades it Daif. The majority (2 of 3) authenticate it.
arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذُنُوبِي وَافْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
english_full: Fatimah the Great narrated:"When Allah's Messenger entered the Masjid he said Salat and Salam upon Muhammad and then said: (Rabbighfirli dhunubi, waftahli abwaba rahmatik) 'O pardon my sins, and open the gates of Your mercy for me.' And when he exited he said Salat and Salam upon Muhammad, and then said: (Rabbighfirli dunubi, waftahli abwaba rakmatik) 'O Lord pardon my sins, and open the gates of Your blessings for me

title: Two lines he said about the verse on minor sins
lede: The Arabic rhymes, which is unusual for him.
translit: In taghfiri-Llāhumma taghfir jammā, wa ayyu ʿabdin laka lā alammā
trans: If You forgive, O Allah, You forgive in abundance. And which servant of Yours has never slipped.
story: The verse describes those who avoid the great sins and the shameful ones, except al-lamam, the small slips. Ibn Abbas reports that this is what the Prophet said about it. It is a question with no possible answer, which is the point.
arabic: إِنْ تَغْفِرِ اللَّهُمَّ تَغْفِرْ جَمَّا وَأَىُّ عَبْدٍ لَكَ لاَ أَلَمَّا
english_full: Narrated 'Ata:from Ibn 'Abbas (regarding this Ayah): Those who avoid great sins and Al-Fawahish except Al-Lamam (minor sins) (53:32). He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Your forgiveness, O Allah is so ample, and which of Your worshipers has not committed Al-Lamam (minor sins)

title: What he said after the traveller had already left
lede: The man never heard this part.
translit: Allāhumma-ṭwi lahu-l-arḍa wa hawwin ʿalayhi-s-safar
trans: O Allah, fold up the earth for him and make the journey easy on him.
story: A man said he was about to travel and asked for advice. He was told to hold to taqwā and say allāhu akbar at every rise in the road. Then he turned to go, and once his back was turned the Prophet said this after him.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اطْوِ لَهُ الأَرْضَ وَهَوِّنْ عَلَيْهِ السَّفَرَ
english_full: Abu Hurairah [may Allah be pleased with him] narrated that :a man said: “O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I intend to travel, so advise me.” He said, “Hold fast to the Taqwa of Allah, and (say the) Takbir upon every elevated place.” So when the man turned away he said: “O Allah make near for him the distance, and ease for him the journey (Allāhummaṭwi lahul-arḍa wa hawwin `alaihis-safar).”

title: The speech most beloved to Allah
lede: Abu Dharr asked plainly and got a short answer.
translit: Mā-ṣṭafā-Llāhu li-malāʾikatih: subḥāna rabbī wa bi-ḥamdih
trans: What Allah chose for His angels: glory to my Lord, and praise to Him.
story: Abu Dharr asked which speech is most beloved to Allah. The answer did not describe a category. It named the exact words He had already picked out for the angels, and handed them over.
arabic: مَا اصْطَفَى اللَّهُ لِمَلاَئِكَتِهِ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي وَبِحَمْدِهِ
english_full: Abu Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) visited him, or that Abu Dharr visited the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said:“May my father and my mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)! Which speech is most beloved to Allah [the Mighty and Sublime]?” So he said: “That which Allah selected for His angels (to say): ‘Glory to my Lord, and with His praise. Glory to my Lord, and with His praise (Subḥāna rabbī wa biḥamdihi, subḥāna rabbī wa biḥamdihi).’”

title: A condition for someone who might not be able to finish
lede: She asked whether she was allowed to make a condition at all.
translit: Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk, wa maḥillī mina-l-arḍi ḥaythu ḥabastanī
trans: Here I am, O Allah, here I am. And my place of release is wherever on the earth You hold me back.
story: Dubāʿah bint az-Zubayr wanted to go for hajj and was not sure her body would carry her through it. She asked if she could set a condition. He said yes, and gave her the wording. Wherever she was stopped would count as the finish line.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Hasan Sahih

arabic: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ وَمَحِلِّي مِنَ الأَرْضِ حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي
english_full: Ibn `Abbas said:Duba`ah, daughter of al-Zubair bin `Abd al-Muttalib, came to the Messenger of Allah(SWAS) and said Messenger of Allah (SWAS) I want to perform Hajj; may I make a provision? He said Yes. She asked how should I say? He replied : Say “ Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik (I am at Thy service, Oh Allah, I am at Thy service). The place where I took off Ihram will be where Thou restrainest me.”

title: Why he called Muadh a man who drives people away
lede: A man walked out of the prayer and prayed alone.
translit: A-fattānun yā Muʿādh, a-fattānun yā Muʿādh
trans: Are you one who drives people to hardship, Muadh? Are you one who drives people to hardship, Muadh?
story: Muadh started al-Baqarah in the maghrib prayer. A man with two watering camels behind him left, prayed on his own and went home. When it reached the Prophet he said this twice, then named the surahs Muadh should have used instead. Sabbiḥisma rabbika-l-aʿlā. Wa-sh-shamsi wa ḍuḥāhā.
arabic: أَفَتَّانٌ يَا مُعَاذُ أَفَتَّانٌ يَا مُعَاذُ
english_full: It was narrated that Jabir said:"A man from among the Ansar passed Mu'adh leading two camels, when he (Mu'adh) was praying maghrib, and he was starting to recite Al-Baqarah. So that man prayed then went away. News of that reached the Prophet (ﷺ) and he said: 'Do you want to cause hardship to the people, O Mu'adh; do you want to cause hardship to the people, O Mu'adh? Why don't you recite: 'Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High' and 'By the sun and its brightness' and the like?

title: The man who kept asking, and was let in
lede: He crawls out, walking once and stumbling once.
translit: Tabāraka-lladhī najjānī mink. Laqad aʿṭāniya-Llāhu shayʾan mā aʿṭāhu aḥadan mina-l-awwalīna wa-l-ākhirīn
trans: Blessed is the One who saved me from you. He has given me something He has not given to anyone before or after.
story: He is the last one out. He asks to be brought near a tree for its shade, promising to ask for nothing else. Then another tree. Then a third, at the gate. He keeps breaking his word and he keeps being given more, until Allah asks what would satisfy him and gives him the world and its like with it.
note: Ibn Masʿūd reports it. In the fuller version Allah laughs at him, and the man asks whether He is mocking him.
arabic: فَقَالَ تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي نَجَّانِي مِنْكِ لَقَدْ أَعْطَانِيَ اللَّهُ شَيْئًا مَا أَعْطَاهُ أَحَدًا مِنَ الأَوَّلِينَ وَالآخِرِينَ
english_full: Ibn Mas'ud reported:Verily the Messenger of Allah said: The last to enter Paradise would be a man who would walk once and stumble once and be burnt by the Fire once. Then when he gets beyond it, he will turn to it and say: Blessed is He Who has saved me from thee. Allah has given me something He has not given to any one of those in earlier or later times. Then a tree would be raised up for him and he will say: O my Lord I bring me near this tree so that I may take shelter in its shade and drink of its water. Allah, the Exalted and Great, would say: O son of Adam, if I grant you this, you will ask Me for something else. He would say: No. my Lord. And he would promise Him that he would not ask for anything else. His Lord would excuse him because He sees what he cannot help desiring; so He would bring him near it, and he would take shelter in its shade and drink of its water. Afterwards a tree more beautiful than the first would be raised up before him and he would say: O my Lord! bring me near this tree in order that I may drink of its water and take shelter in its shade and I shall not ask Thee for anything else. He (Allah) would say: O son of Adam, if I bring you near it you may ask me for something else. He would promise Him that he would not ask for anything else. His Lord will excuse him because He would see something he cannot help desiring. So He would bring him near it and he would enjoy its shade and drink its water. Then a tree would be raised up for him at the gate of the Paradise, more beautiful than the first two. He would say: O my Lord! bring me near this (tree) so that I may enjoy its shade and drink from its water. I shall not ask Thee for anything else. He (Allah) would say: O son of Adam! did you not promise Me that you would not ask Me anything else? He would say: Yes, my Lord, but I shall not ask Thee for anything else. His Lord would excuse him for He sees something the temptation of which he could not resist. He (Allah) would bring him near to it, and when He would bring him near it he would hear the voices of the inhabitants of the Paradise. He would say: O my Lord! admit me to it. He (Allah) would say: O son of Adam, what will bring an end to your requests to Me? Will it please you if I give you the whole world and a like one along with it? He will say: O my Lord! art Thou mocking at me, though Thou art the Lord of the worlds? Ibn Mas'ud laughed and asked (the hearers): Why don't you ask me what I am laughing at. They (then) said: Why do you laugh? He said: It is in this way that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed. They (the companions of the Holy Prophet) asked: Why do you laugh. Messenger of Allah? He said: On account of the laugh of the Lord of the universe, when he ldesirer of Paradise) sai Thou mocking at me though Thou art the Lord of the worlds? He would say: I am not mocking at you, but I have power to do whatever I will

title: What he will say at the Basin about people he recognises
lede: Ibn Abi Mulaykah started praying against it out loud.
translit: Fa-aqūlu yā rabbi minnī wa min ummatī
trans: So I will say: my Lord, they are from me and from my community.
story: He said he would be at the Basin watching who came, and people would be taken away in front of him, and he would object on their behalf. The answer is that he does not know what they did after he left. Asma bint Abi Bakr reported it, and the narrator after her could not hear it without saying: O Allah, we seek refuge in You from turning back on our heels.
arabic: فَأَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ مِنِّي وَمِنْ أُمَّتِي
english_full: Narrated Asma 'bint Abu Bakr:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I will be standing at the Lake-Fount so that I will see whom among you will come to me; and some people will be taken away from me, and I will say, 'O Lord, (they are) from me and from my followers.' Then it will be said, 'Did you notice what they did after you? By Allah, they kept on turning on their heels (turned as renegades).' " The sub-narrator, Ibn Abi Mulaika said, "O Allah, we seek refuge with You from turning on our heels, or being put to trial in our religion

title: The one case where saying more than you know is not lying
lede: Narrated by a woman through her son.
translit: Laysa bi-l-kādhibi man aṣlaḥa bayna-n-nāsi fa-qāla khayran aw namā khayrā
trans: He is not a liar who puts things right between people, saying something good or passing on something good.
story: Namā means to carry a report from one side to the other. Ordinarily that is the word used for the gossip that breaks people apart. Here it is the same verb doing the opposite job, and the ruling on it is reversed with it.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih
Zubair Ali Zai: Sahih Bukhari (2692) Sahih Muslim (2605)

arabic: لَيْسَ بِالْكَاذِبِ مَنْ أَصْلَحَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فَقَالَ خَيْرًا أَوْ نَمَى خَيْرًا
english_full: Humaid b. 'Abd al-Rahman quoted his mother as saying:The Prophet (ﷺ) said: He who forged in order to put things right between two persons did not lie. The version by Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Musaddad has: The liar is not the one who puts things right between people, saying what is good and increasing good

title: Why he told them to stop cursing their own children
lede: The reason given is not that it is unkind.
translit: Lā tadʿū ʿalā anfusikum, wa lā tadʿū ʿalā awlādikum, wa lā tadʿū ʿalā khadamikum, wa lā tadʿū ʿalā amwālikum. Lā tuwāfiqū mina-Llāhi sāʿata naylin fīhā ʿaṭāʾun fa-yastajība lakum
trans: Do not pray against yourselves, or against your children, or against those who serve you, or against your property. Do not let it land on an hour from Allah in which giving is happening, and He answers you.
story: The warning is not about temper. It is about timing. Something said in exhaustion at the wrong minute of the day could be taken up and granted, and the thing you said in a bad hour becomes the thing you have to live with.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: لاَ تَدْعُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ وَلاَ تَدْعُوا عَلَى أَوْلاَدِكُمْ وَلاَ تَدْعُوا عَلَى خَدَمِكُمْ وَلاَ تَدْعُوا عَلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ لاَ تُوَافِقُوا مِنَ اللَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى سَاعَةَ نَيْلٍ فِيهَا عَطَاءٌ فَيَسْتَجِيبَ لَكُمْ
english_full: Jabir b. 'Abd Allah reported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as saying:Do not invoke curse on yourselves, and do not invoke curse on your children, and do not invoke curse on your servants, and do not invoke curse on your property, lest you happen to do it at a time when Allah is asked for something and grants your request. Abu Dawud said: This Hadith has a continuous chain of narrators, 'Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin 'Ubadah (did) met Jabir

title: Aisha weeping at Sarif
lede: She said she wished she had never set out.
translit: Innamā dhālika shayʾun kataba-Llāhu ʿalā banāti Ādam
trans: That is only something Allah has written for the daughters of Adam.
story: They had raised their voices in talbiyah for hajj. At Sarif she got her period, and he came in and found her crying, and asked why. She said: I wish I had never come. He said this, and then told her to perform every rite of the pilgrimage except circling the House.
note: Nothing was cancelled. One thing was set aside.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: إِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ شَىْءٌ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى بَنَاتِ آدَمَ
english_full: Ai’shah said :We raised our voices in talbiyah for Hajj. When we reached Sarif, I menstruated. The Messenger of Allah (SWAS) came upon me while I was weeping. He asked, why are your weeping, Ai’shah? I replied, I menstruated. Would that I had not come out for performing Hajj. He said : Glory be to Allah, this is a thing prescribed by Allah on the daughters of Adam. He said perform all the rites of Hajj but do not go round the House (the Ka’bah). When we entered Makkah, the Messenger of Allah (SWAS) said he who desires to make (his Hajj) an `Umrah may do so, except those who have sacrificial animals with them. The Messenger of Allah (SWAS) sacrificed a cow on behalf of his wives on the day of sacrifice. When the night of al-Batha came, and Ai’shah was purified she said to the Messenger of Allah (SWAS) my fellow female pilgrims will return after performing Hajj and `Umrah and I shall return after performing only Hajj? He therefore, ordered `Abd al-Rahman bin Abu Bakr who took her to al-Ta’nim. She uttered there talbiyah for `Umrah

title: People brought to the Garden in chains
lede: One line, and no explanation attached to it.
translit: Laqad ʿajiba rabbunā min qawmin yuqādūna ilā-l-jannati fi-s-salāsil
trans: Our Lord marvels at a people led to the Garden in chains.
story: They were captives, taken against their will, and what they found at the end of the road was the thing they would have chosen if they had known. The chains are real. So is where they lead.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: لَقَدْ عَجِبَ رَبُّنَا عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ يُقَادُونَ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ فِي السَّلاَسِلِ
english_full: Abu Hurairah reported the Apostle of Allaah(ﷺ) as saying “Our Lord Most High is charmed with people who will be led to Paradise in chains.”

title: What he said at each end of the day
lede: The evening version drops one word.
translit: Allāhumma bika aṣbaḥnā wa bika amsaynā wa bika naḥyā wa bika namūt wa ilayka-n-nushūr
trans: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the rising.
story: Four things are put under the same preposition. Morning, evening, living, dying. In the evening he left out the word for morning, because it had already happened.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا وَبِكَ نَحْيَا وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
english_full: Narrated AbuHurayrah: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say in the morning: "O Allah, by Thee we come to the morning, by Thee we come to the evening, by Thee are we resurrected." In the evening he would say: "O Allah, by Thee we come to the evening, by Thee we die, and to Thee are we resurrected

title: Three things to be content with
lede: The consequence attached to it is unusually short.
translit: Man qāla: raḍītu bi-Llāhi rabban wa bi-l-islāmi dīnan wa bi-Muḥammadin rasūlā, wajabat lahu-l-jannah
trans: Whoever says: I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger, Paradise becomes due for him.
story: Wajabat is a word from contracts. It means the thing has fallen due, become owed. Not hoped for. Not likely. Owed.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: مَنْ قَالَ رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا وَبِالإِسْلاَمِ دِينًا وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ رَسُولاً وَجَبَتْ لَهُ الْجَنَّةُ
english_full: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as saying:If anyone says "I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muhammad (ﷺ) as Apostle" Paradise will be his due

title: What seals a gathering
lede: Said three times on standing up, and it works both ways.
translit: Subḥānaka-Llāhumma wa bi-ḥamdika, lā ilāha illā ant, astaghfiruka wa atūbu ilayk
trans: Glory to You, O Allah, and praise. There is no god but You. I ask Your forgiveness and I turn back to You.
story: If the gathering was a waste, these words cover what was said in it. If the gathering was good, they seal it the way wax is stamped on a document. The same sentence does two different jobs depending on the room you are leaving.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ
english_full: Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As: There are some expressions which a man utters three times when he gets up from an assembly he will be forgiven for what happened in the assembly; and no one utters them in an assembly held for a noble cause or for remembrance of Allah but that is stamped with them just as a document is stamped with a signet-ring. These expressions are: Glory be to Thee, O Allah, and I begin with praise of Thee, there is no god but thou; I ask Thy pardon, and return to Thee in repentance

title: A prayer for the sick with a reason attached
lede: It asks for recovery and then says what the recovery is for.
translit: Allāhumma-shfi ʿabdaka yankaʾu laka ʿaduwwan aw yamshī laka ilā janāzah
trans: O Allah, heal Your servant, that he may wound an enemy for You, or walk to a funeral for You.
story: Two ordinary uses for a working body, one at either end of the scale. Standing against something, or walking somewhere on foot for someone else. One narration of the same hadith has walking to the prayer in place of the funeral.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اشْفِ عَبْدَكَ يَنْكَأُ لَكَ عَدُوًّا أَوْ يَمْشِي لَكَ إِلَى جَنَازَةٍ
english_full: Narrated Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: When a man comes to visit a sick person, he should say: O Allah, cure Thy servant, who may then wreak havoc on an enemy for your sake, or walk at a funeral for your sake. Abu Dawud said: Ibn As-Sarh (one of the narrators) said: "Ilas-salat (To the Salat)

title: The first thing created, and what it was told
lede: Ubadah told his son this to explain what belief tastes like.
translit: Qāla rabbi wa mādhā aktub. Qāla: uktub maqādīra kulli shayʾin ḥattā taqūma-s-sāʿah
trans: It said: my Lord, what shall I write? He said: write the measures of everything, until the Hour comes.
story: Ubadah ibn as-Samit said to his son: you will never taste the reality of faith until you know that what reached you could not have missed you, and what missed you could not have reached you. Then he gave the hadith as his evidence.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ وَمَاذَا أَكْتُبُ قَالَ اكْتُبْ مَقَادِيرَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ حَتَّى تَقُومَ السَّاعَةُ
english_full: Ubadah b. al Samit said to his son :Son! You will not get the taste of the reality of faith until you know that what has come to you could not miss you, and that what has missed you could not come to you. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It asked: What should I write, my Lord? He said: Write what was decreed about everything till the Last Hour comes. Son! I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say : He who dies on something other than this does not belong to me

title: What he corrected when the animal stumbled
lede: The rider had said the obvious thing.
translit: Lā taqul: taʿisa-sh-shayṭān. Fa-innaka idhā qulta dhālika taʿāẓama ḥattā yakūna mithla-l-bayti wa yaqūla bi-quwwatī. Wa lākin qul: bismi-Llāh. Fa-innaka idhā qulta dhālika taṣāghara ḥattā yakūna mithla-dh-dhubāb
trans: Do not say: may Satan perish. If you say that he swells until he is the size of a house and says, by my power. But say: in the name of Allah. If you say that he shrinks until he is the size of a fly.
story: The man was riding behind him and the animal tripped, and he cursed the devil, which sounds like the pious response. He was told it is the opposite. Naming him as the cause is the credit he wants.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: لاَ تَقُلْ تَعِسَ الشَّيْطَانُ فَإِنَّكَ إِذَا قُلْتَ ذَلِكَ تَعَاظَمَ حَتَّى يَكُونَ مِثْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيَقُولَ بِقُوَّتِي وَلَكِنْ قُلْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّكَ إِذَا قُلْتَ ذَلِكَ تَصَاغَرَ حَتَّى يَكُونَ مِثْلَ الذُّبَابِ
english_full: Abu al-Malih reported on the authority of a man :I was riding on a mount behind the prophet (May peace be upon him). It stumbled. Thereupon I said: May the devil perish! He said: do not say; may the devil perish! For you say that, he will swell so much so that he will be like a house, and say: by my power. But say: in the name of Allah; for when you say that, he will diminish so much so that he will be like a fly

title: The limit on not speaking to someone
lede: And who carries the sin once it goes past that.
translit: Lā yakūnu li-muslimin an yahjura musliman fawqa thalāthah. Fa-idhā laqiyahu sallama ʿalayhi thalātha mirārin kullu dhālika lā yaruddu ʿalayhi faqad bāʾa bi-ithmih
trans: It is not for a Muslim to cut off another Muslim beyond three days. If he meets him and greets him three times and gets no reply each time, the other has taken the sin on himself.
story: It gives the person who wants to fix it a way out that does not require an apology or a conversation. Say salām. Three times. After that it is not yours any more.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Hasan

arabic: لاَ يَكُونُ لِمُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَهْجُرَ مُسْلِمًا فَوْقَ ثَلاَثَةٍ فَإِذَا لَقِيَهُ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلاَثَ مِرَارٍ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لاَ يَرُدُّ عَلَيْهِ فَقَدْ بَاءَ بِإِثْمِهِ
english_full: Narrated Aisha, Ummul Mu'minin: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: It is not right for a Muslim to keep apart from another Muslim for more than three days. Then when he meets him and gives three salutations, receiving during that time no response, the other bears his sin

title: Who he included in his own sacrifice
lede: He said it with the knife in his hand.
translit: Bismi-Llāhi wa-Llāhu akbar. Hādhā ʿannī wa ʿamman lam yuḍaḥḥi min ummatī
trans: In the name of Allah, and Allah is greatest. This is from me, and from whoever of my community did not sacrifice.
story: Jabir was there. He came down from the pulpit after the sermon, a ram was brought, and he slaughtered it himself, and then he named a second group with no faces and no numbers: everyone who could not afford one.
dissent: Scholars differ on this chain. Zubair Ali Zai grades it Daif. The majority (2 of 3) authenticate it.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ هَذَا عَنِّي وَعَمَّنْ لَمْ يُضَحِّ مِنْ أُمَّتِي
english_full: Narrated Jabir ibn Abdullah: I witnessed sacrificing along with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the place of prayer. When he finished his sermon, he descended from his pulpit, and a ram was brought to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slaughtered it with his hand, and said: In the name of Allah, Allah, is Most Great. This is from me and from those who did not sacrifice from my community

title: A one word correction
lede: The difference is between and, and then.
translit: Fa-lā yaqul: mā shāʾa-Llāhu wa shiʾt. Wa lākin li-yaqul: mā shāʾa-Llāhu thumma shiʾt
trans: Let him not say: what Allah wills and what you will. Let him say: what Allah wills, then what you will.
story: Wa puts two things side by side. Thumma puts one after the other. The whole correction is one particle, and it moves a human being out of a position he was never in.

gradings: Muhammad Fouad Abd al-Baqi: Hasan Sahih

arabic: فَلاَ يَقُلْ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ وَشِئْتَ وَلَكِنْ لِيَقُلْ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ شِئْتَ
english_full: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:'When anyone of you swears an oath, let him not say: 'What Allah wills and what you will.' Rather let him say: 'What Allah wills and then what you will

title: What he asked to be kept among
lede: Abu Saʿid heard him say it and drew the obvious instruction from it.
translit: Allāhumma aḥyinī miskīnan wa amitnī miskīnan wa-ḥshurnī fī zumrati-l-masākīn
trans: O Allah, let me live poor, let me die poor, and gather me in the company of the poor.
story: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri opened with an instruction of his own before quoting it: love the poor. Then he gave the reason, which is that the Prophet asked to be counted as one of them at all three points, living, dying and standing up again.
dissent: Scholars differ on this chain. Zubair Ali Zai grades it Daif. The majority (2 of 3) authenticate it.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَحْيِنِي مِسْكِينًا وَأَمِتْنِي مِسْكِينًا وَاحْشُرْنِي فِي زُمْرَةِ الْمَسَاكِينِ
english_full: It was narrated that Abu Sa’eed Al-Khudri said:“Love the poor, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say in his supplication: ‘O Allah, cause me to live poor and cause me to die poor, and gather me among the poor (on the Day of Resurrection).’”

title: What he said with his finger for someone in pain
lede: Dust from the ground and saliva from the person.
translit: Bismi-Llāh, bi-turbati arḍinā, bi-rīqati baʿḍinā, li-yushfā saqīmunā bi-idhni rabbinā
trans: In the name of Allah. With the dust of our land, with the saliva of one of us, may our sick one be healed by the permission of our Lord.
story: Aisha describes the gesture. Finger touched to the ground, then to his own mouth, then to the place that hurt. Two of the most ordinary substances on earth, and then the clause that does the actual work.

gradings: Zubair Ali Zai: Sahih - Agreed Upon

arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ بِتُرْبَةِ أَرْضِنَا بِرِيقَةِ بَعْضِنَا لِيُشْفَى سَقِيمُنَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّنَا
english_full: It was narrated from ‘Aishah that one of the things that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say for the sick person, with saliva on his finger (dipped in dust), was:“Bismillah, turbatu ardina, biriqati ba’dina, liyushfa saqimuna. Bi’dhni Rabbina (In the Name of Allah, the dust of our land mixed with the saliva of one of us, to cure our sick one by the permission of our Lord).”

title: What the ground says about the person buried in it
lede: It explains why a need takes you somewhere.
translit: Fa-taqūlu-l-arḍu yawma-l-qiyāmah: rabbi hādhā mā-stawdaʿtanī
trans: On the Day of Resurrection the earth will say: my Lord, this is what You left with me.
story: If your appointed time is in a certain land, some errand will make you go there, and when you reach the furthest point of your track you are taken. The ground is described as holding a deposit, and returning it with a sentence like a receipt.
dissent: Scholars differ on this chain. Zubair Ali Zai grades it Daif. The majority (2 of 3) authenticate it.
arabic: فَتَقُولُ الأَرْضُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ رَبِّ هَذَا مَا اسْتَوْدَعْتَنِي
english_full: It was narrated from ‘Abdullah bin Mas’ud that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:“If the appointed time of death of anyone of you is in a certain land, some need will cause him to go there, then when he reaches the furthest point that it is decreed he will reach, Allah takes (his soul). And on the Day of Resurrection the earth will say: ‘My Lord, this is what You entrusted to me.’”

title: What his Lord promised him about his community
lede: He swore on it before he said it.
translit: Wa laqad waʿadanī rabbī an yudkhila-l-jannata min ummatī sabʿīna alfan bi-ghayri ḥisāb
trans: My Lord has promised me that seventy thousand of my community will enter the Garden with no reckoning.
story: He began: by the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no servant believes and then holds steady but that he is walked into the Garden. Then he said he hoped they would not enter before his listeners and the righteous among their children had taken their places in it.
arabic: وَلَقَدْ وَعَدَنِي رَبِّي عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَنْ يُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي سَبْعِينَ أَلْفًا بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
english_full: It was narrated that Rifa’ah Al-Juhani said:“We came back (from a campaign) with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, there is no person who believes then stands firm, but he will be caused to enter Paradise. I hope that they will not enter it until you and those who are righteous among your offspring will enter it and take up your dwelling places therein. And my Lord has promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account.’”

title: What al-Fatihah is called
lede: Three names in one line.
translit: Al-ḥamdu lillāhi ummu-l-qurʾāni wa ummu-l-kitābi wa-s-sabʿu-l-mathānī
trans: Al-hamdu lillah is the mother of the Qurʾān, the mother of the Book, and the seven oft repeated.
story: Umm in Arabic is the origin something returns to, the source a thing is traced back to. Seven verses, said at least seventeen times a day, and named as the place the rest comes from.
arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ أُمُّ الْقُرْآنِ وَأُمُّ الْكِتَابِ وَالسَّبْعُ الْمَثَانِي
english_full: Narrated Abu Hurairah:that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Hamdulillah is Umm Al-Qur'an and Umm Al-Kitab and the seven oft-repeated

title: What he said after gathering them under a cloak
lede: Umar ibn Abi Salamah was in the house and saw it.
translit: Allāhumma hāʾulāʾi ahlu baytī fa-adhhib ʿanhumu-r-rijsa wa ṭahhirhum taṭhīrā
trans: O Allah, these are the people of my house. Remove impurity from them and purify them completely.
story: The verse came down in Umm Salamah's house. He called Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, wrapped them in a cloak, with Ali behind him, wrapped him too, and then prayed the words of the verse back over them.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ هَؤُلاَءِ أَهْلُ بَيْتِي فَأَذْهِبْ عَنْهُمُ الرِّجْسَ وَطَهِّرْهُمْ تَطْهِيرًا
english_full: Narrated 'Umar bin Abi Salamah - the step-son of the Prophet (ﷺ):"When these Ayat were revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Allah only wishes to remove the Rijs from you, O members of the family, and to purify you with a thorough purification (33:33)' in the home of Umm Salamah, he called for Fatimah, Hasan, Husain, and wrapped him in the cloak, and 'Ali was behind him, so he wrapped him in the cloak, then he said: 'O Allah! These are the people of my house, so remove the Rijs from them, and purify them with a thorough purification.' So Umm Salamah said: 'And I, Prophet of Allah?' He said: 'You are in your place (meaning you are already a member of my household), and you are goodness

title: Two words he said when people came asking on behalf of others
lede: The permission is given before the outcome is known.
translit: Ishfaʿū tushaffaʿū, wa yaqḍi-Llāhu ʿalā lisāni nabiyyihi mā shāʾ
trans: Intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. And Allah decides on the tongue of His Prophet whatever He wills.
story: Someone would come needing something and he would turn to the people around him and tell them to speak up for the person. The reward was in the asking. The outcome was never theirs to determine, and he said so in the same breath.

gradings: Zubair Ali Zai: Sahih - Agreed Upon

arabic: اشْفَعُوا تُشَفَّعُوا وَيَقْضِي اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَلَى لِسَانِ نَبِيِّهِ مَا شَاءَ
english_full: It was narrated from Abu Musa that the Prophet said:"Intercede and your intercession may be accepted, and Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, decrees on the lips of His Prophet whatsoever He will

title: A prayer someone asked for and could use
lede: Five things, all of them his own.
translit: Allāhumma ʿāfinī min sharri samʿī wa baṣarī wa lisānī wa qalbī
trans: O Allah, keep me safe from the evil of my hearing, my sight, my tongue and my heart.
story: He said: teach me a supplication I can benefit from. Not one about enemies, or debt, or illness. Every item on the list is a part of himself he already owns and cannot put down.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ عَافِنِي مِنْ شَرِّ سَمْعِي وَبَصَرِي وَلِسَانِي وَقَلْبِي
english_full: It was narrated from Shutair bin Shakal bin Humaid, that his father said:"I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication from which I may benefit.' He said: 'Say: Allahumma 'afini min sharri sam'i, wa basari, wa lisani, wa qalbi, wa sharri mani (O Allah, protect me from the evil of my hearing, my seeing, my tongue and my heart, and the evil of my sperm.)" - Meaning his sexual organ

title: What he said weeping in prostration during the eclipse
lede: He was holding Allah to something already written.
translit: Rabbi lam taʿidnī hādhā wa anā astaghfiruk, lam taʿidnī hādhā wa anā fīhim
trans: My Lord, did You not promise me that You would not do this while I am asking Your forgiveness? Did You not promise me this while I am among them?
story: The sun went dark and he prayed a long standing, a long bowing, a long prostration, and Abdullah ibn Amr says he was weeping and blowing in his prostration, saying this. He was reciting back to Allah the verse that says punishment does not come while the Prophet is among them and while they seek forgiveness.
note: The verse is al-Anfāl 8:33.
arabic: رَبِّ لَمْ تَعِدْنِي هَذَا وَأَنَا أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ لَمْ تَعِدْنِي هَذَا وَأَنَا فِيهِمْ
english_full: It was narrated that Abdullah bin Amr said:"The sun eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed and stood for a long time, then he bowed for a long time, then he stood up and (remained standing) for a long time." (One of the narrators) Shu'bh said: "I think he said something similar concerning prostration."- "He started weeping and blowing during his prostration and said: 'Lord, You did not tell me that You would do that while I am asking You for forgiveness; You did not tell me that You would do that while I was still among them.' When he finished praying he said: "Paradise was shown to me, and if I had stretched forth my hand I could have taken some of its fruits. And Hell was shown to me, so I started blowing for fear that its heat might overwhelm you. I saw therein the thief who stole the two camels of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); and I saw therein the brother of Banu As-Du'du; the thief who stole from the pilgrims, and when he was caught he said: The crooked stick did it; and I saw therein a tall black woman who was being punished because of a cat she tied up and did not feed or give it water, and she did not let it eat of the vermin of the earth, until it died. Then sun and the moon do not become eclipsed for the death or birth of anyone, but they are two of the signs of Allah. If one of them becomes eclipsed'- or he said: 'if one of them does anything like that'- 'then hasten to remember Allah, the Mighty and Sublime

title: What he said when he repaid a loan
lede: He had borrowed forty thousand.
translit: Bāraka-Llāhu laka fī ahlika wa mālik. Innamā jazāʾu-s-salafi-l-ḥamdu wa-l-adāʾ
trans: May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth. The repayment of a loan is thanks and settlement.
story: The lender reported it himself. Money came in, the Prophet handed the whole amount back, and then added the sentence, which sets out what a lender is actually owed. The sum, and being thanked for it.
arabic: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ فِي أَهْلِكَ وَمَالِكَ إِنَّمَا جَزَاءُ السَّلَفِ الْحَمْدُ وَالأَدَاءُ
english_full: it was narrated from Isla'il bin Ibrahim bin 'Abdullah bin Abi Rabi'ah, from his father, that his grandfather said:"The Prophet borrowed forty thousand from me, then some wealth came to him, and he paid me back and said: 'May Allah bless your family and your wealth for you: the reward for lending is praise and repayment

title: What is written before anyone is born
lede: The list is short and the last line is the hard one.
translit: Wa yuktabu ʿamaluhu wa atharuhu wa ajaluhu wa rizquh, thumma tuṭwa-ṣ-ṣuḥufu fa-lā yuzādu fīhā wa lā yunqaṣ
trans: His deeds are written, and his trace, and his term, and his provision. Then the pages are folded, and nothing is added to them and nothing taken away.
story: The angel comes to the drop after forty or forty five nights and asks two questions, and both answers are written. Then four more things are entered. Athar is the mark a person leaves behind after he is gone, and it is recorded before he arrives.
arabic: وَيُكْتَبُ عَمَلُهُ وَأَثَرُهُ وَأَجَلُهُ وَرِزْقُهُ ثُمَّ تُطْوَى الصُّحُفُ فَلاَ يُزَادُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يُنْقَصُ
english_full: Hudhaifa b. Usaid reported directly from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) that he said:When the drop of (semen) remains in the womb for forty or forty five nights, the angel comes and says: My Lord, will he be good or evil? And both these things would be written. Then the angel says: My Lord, would he be male or female? And both these things are written. And his deeds and actions, his death, his livelihood; these are also recorded. Then his document of destiny is rolled and there is no addition to nor subtraction from it

title: What he said when he asked for rain
lede: People come before animals, and land comes last.
translit: Allāhumma-sqi ʿibādaka wa bahīmatak, wa-nshur raḥmatak, wa aḥyi baladaka-l-mayyit
trans: O Allah, water Your servants and Your animals, spread Your mercy, and bring Your dead land back to life.
story: Every noun in it is possessive and none of them are his. Your servants, Your animals, Your mercy, Your land. He is not asking for something to be given to him. He is asking for something to be given back to what it belongs to.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اسْقِ عِبَادَكَ وَبَهِيمَتَكَ وَانْشُرْ رَحْمَتَكَ وَأَحْىِ بَلَدَكَ الْمَيِّتَ
english_full: Yahya related to me from Malik from Yahya ibn Said from Amr ibn Shuayb that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, when he asked for rain, "O Allah, give water to Your slaves and Your animals, and spread Your mercy, and give life to Your dead land

title: When the rain would not stop
lede: A week earlier the same man had come asking for it.
translit: Allāhumma ẓuhūra-l-jibāli wa-l-ākām, wa buṭūna-l-awdiyah, wa manābita-sh-shajar
trans: O Allah, on the ridges of the mountains and the hills, in the beds of the valleys, and where the trees grow.
story: A man came saying the livestock were dying and the roads were cut, so he asked, and it rained from one Friday to the next. Then a man came saying the houses had collapsed and the roads were cut and the livestock were dying. He did not ask for it to stop. He asked for it to be moved.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ ظُهُورَ الْجِبَالِ وَالآكَامِ وَبُطُونَ الأَوْدِيَةِ وَمَنَابِتَ الشَّجَرِ
english_full: Yahya related to me from Malik from Sharik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namir that Anas ibn Malik said, "A man came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, 'Messenger of Allah, our animals are dying and our camels are too weak to travel, so make dua to Allah.' The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made dua, and it rained on us from one jumua to the next." Anas continued, "Then a man came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, 'Messenger of Allah, our houses have fallen down, the paths are blocked, and our flocks are dying.' The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, 'O Allah, (only) the mountain and hill-tops, the valley bottoms, and the places where trees grow.' " Anas added, "It cleared away from Madina like a garment being removed." Malik said, about a man who missed the prayer of asking for rain but caught the khutba, and wished to pray in the mosque, or in his house when he returned, "He is free to do so, or not, as he wishes

title: A prophet wiping blood off his face
lede: Ibn Masʿud said he could still picture him telling it.
translit: Rabbi-ghfir li-qawmī fa-innahum lā yaʿlamūn
trans: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.
story: He was describing an earlier prophet whose own people had beaten him. Ibn Masʿud says it was as if he could see the Messenger of Allah doing it, the hand moving over the face, the blood coming away, and the sentence being said while it was still happening.
arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِقَوْمِي فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ
english_full: It has been narrated on the authority of 'Abdullah who said:It appeared to me as if I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (and heard him) relate the story of a Prophet who had been beaten by his people, was wiping the blood from his face and was saying. My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know

title: What Umm Sulaym asked for instead of anything for herself
lede: She had one small request left after he had prayed for her household.
translit: Allāhumma-rzuqhu mālan wa waladan wa bārik lah
trans: O Allah, give him wealth and children, and bless him in it.
story: He visited, refused the dates and ghee because he was fasting, prayed a voluntary prayer in the corner of the house and then made duʿā for her and her family. She said: I have one little request. He asked what. She said: your servant, Anas. Anas himself is the one narrating, and he ends it by noting that he became one of the wealthiest of the Ansar.
note: The third clause is the one people leave off. Wealth and children, and then barakah in them.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْهُ مَالاً وَوَلَدًا وَبَارِكْ لَهُ
english_full: Narrated Anas:The Prophet (ﷺ) paid a visit to Um-Sulaim and she placed before him dates and ghee. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Replace the ghee and dates in their respective containers for I am fasting." Then he stood somewhere in her house and offered an optional prayer and then he invoked good on Um-Sulaim and her family. Then Um-Sulaim said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! I have a special request (today)." He said, "What is it?" She replied, "(Please invoke for) your servant Anas." So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did not leave anything good in the world or the Hereafter which he did not invoke (Allah to bestow) on me and said, "O Allah! Give him (i.e. Anas) property and children and bless him." Thus I am one of the richest among the Ansar and my daughter Umaina told me that when Al-Hajjaj came to Basra, more than 120 of my offspring had been buried

title: The private conversation on that Day
lede: A man asked Ibn Umar what he had heard about it.
translit: Innī satartu ʿalayka fi-d-dunyā, fa-anā aghfiruhā laka-l-yawm
trans: I covered it for you in the world, and today I forgive it for you.
story: One of you will be brought near his Lord until He puts His screen over him. Then: you did such and such. He says yes. You did such and such. He says yes. He is made to admit all of it, and then told this. The screen was already there while he was alive and he never knew.
arabic: إِنِّي سَتَرْتُ عَلَيْكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا، فَأَنَا أَغْفِرُهَا لَكَ الْيَوْمَ
english_full: Narrated Safwan bin Muhriz:A man asked Ibn `Umar, "What did you hear Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying regarding An-Najwa (secret talk between Allah and His believing worshipper on the Day of Judgment)?" He said, "(The Prophet (ﷺ) said), "One of you will come close to his Lord till He will shelter him in His screen and say: Did you commit such-and-such sin? He will say, 'Yes.' Then Allah will say: Did you commit such and such sin? He will say, 'Yes.' So Allah will make him confess (all his sins) and He will say, 'I screened them (your sins) for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you

title: The promise he took out for people he might wrong
lede: He began by saying what he is.
translit: Allāhumma innī attakhidhu ʿindaka ʿahdan lan tukhlifanīh. Fa-innamā anā bashar. Fa-ayyu-l-muʾminīna ādhaytuhu, shatamtuhu, laʿantuhu, jaladtuhu, fa-jʿalhā lahu ṣalātan wa zakātan wa qurbatan tuqarribuhu bihā ilayka yawma-l-qiyāmah
trans: O Allah, I take a covenant with You that You will not break with me. I am only a human being. So any believer I have harmed, or insulted, or cursed, or struck, make it for him a prayer and a purification and a nearness that brings him close to You on the Day of Resurrection.
story: He is arranging in advance for the people he might wrong. Not asking to be forgiven for it. Asking that the injury itself be converted into something that works in their favour on the day it would otherwise be counted against him.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَتَّخِذُ عِنْدَكَ عَهْدًا لَنْ تُخْلِفَنِيهِ فَإِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ فَأَىُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ آذَيْتُهُ شَتَمْتُهُ لَعَنْتُهُ جَلَدْتُهُ فَاجْعَلْهَا لَهُ صَلاَةً وَزَكَاةً وَقُرْبَةً تُقَرِّبُهُ بِهَا إِلَيْكَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
english_full: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying:O Allah, I make a covenant with Thee against which Thou wouldst never go. I am a human being and thus for a Muslim whom I give any harm or whom I scold or upon whom I invoke curse or whom I beat, make this a source of blessing, purification and nearness to Thee on the Day of Resurrection

title: What he was chanting while carrying earth at the Trench
lede: Al-Bara says the dust had covered the hair on his chest.
translit: Allāhumma lawlā anta mā-htadaynā wa lā taṣaddaqnā wa lā ṣallaynā. Fa-anzilan sakīnatan ʿalaynā wa thabbiti-l-aqdāma in lāqaynā
trans: O Allah, were it not for You we would not have been guided, nor given in charity, nor prayed. So send down calm upon us, and hold our feet firm if we meet them.
story: A siege, a ditch being dug by hand, and the Prophet carrying earth with everyone else until he was covered in it. The lines are Abdullah ibn Rawahah's, and al-Bara says he was raising his voice with them.
note: Sakīnah before firmness. Calm first, then the feet.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ لَوْلاَ أَنْتَ مَا اهْتَدَيْنَا وَلاَ تَصَدَّقْنَا وَلاَ صَلَّيْنَا فَأَنْزِلَنْ سَكِينَةً عَلَيْنَا وَثَبِّتِ الأَقْدَامَ إِنْ لاَقَيْنَا
