title: What he made inviolable in the farewell sermon
lede: He measured it against the day they were standing in.
translit: Fa-inna dimāʾakum wa amwālakum wa aʿrāḍakum baynakum ḥarāmun ka-ḥurmati yawmikum hādhā, fī shahrikum hādhā, fī baladikum hādhā
trans: Your blood, your property and your honour are sacred among you, like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours.
story: They were standing in the most protected day, in the most protected month, in the most protected place. He pointed at all three and said: this is what a person is worth. Then: let the one present carry it to the one absent.
arabic: فَإِنَّ دِمَاءَكُمْ وَأَمْوَالَكُمْ وَأَعْرَاضَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ حَرَامٌ كَحُرْمَةِ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا، فِي شَهْرِكُمْ هَذَا، فِي بَلَدِكُمْ هَذَا
english_full: Narrated `Abdur-Rahman bin Abi Bakra's father:Once the Prophet (ﷺ) was riding his camel and a man was holding its rein. The Prophet (ﷺ) asked, "What is the day today?" We kept quiet, thinking that he might give that day another name. He said, "Isn't it the day of Nahr (slaughtering of the animals of sacrifice)" We replied, "Yes." He further asked, "Which month is this?" We again kept quiet, thinking that he might give it another name. Then he said, "Isn't it the month of Dhul-Hijja?" We replied, "Yes." He said, "Verily! Your blood, property and honor are sacred to one another (i.e. Muslims) like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours and in this city of yours. It is incumbent upon those who are present to inform those who are absent because those who are absent might comprehend (what I have said) better than the present audience

title: The sign that Allah wants good for someone
lede: He put himself in the sentence as the one who distributes.
translit: Man yuridi-Llāhu bihi khayran yufaqqihhu fi-d-dīn, wa innamā anā qāsimun wa-Llāhu yuʿṭī
trans: Whoever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding in the religion. I am only one who distributes, and Allah is the one who gives.
story: Not knowledge. Fiqh, which is the understanding that lets a person work out what they have not been told. And the second clause separates the hand it comes through from the source it comes from.
arabic: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ، وَإِنَّمَا أَنَا قَاسِمٌ وَاللَّهُ يُعْطِي
english_full: Narrated Muawiya:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If Allah wants to do good to a person, He makes him comprehend the religion. I am just a distributor, but the grant is from Allah. (And remember) that this nation (true Muslims) will keep on following Allah's teachings strictly and they will not be harmed by any one going on a different path till Allah's order (Day of Judgment) is established

title: How knowledge actually disappears
lede: It is not pulled out of anybody.
translit: Inna-Llāha lā yaqbiḍu-l-ʿilma-ntizāʿan yantaziʿuhu mina-l-ʿibād, wa lākin yaqbiḍu-l-ʿilma bi-qabḍi-l-ʿulamāʾ, ḥattā idhā lam yubqi ʿāliman
trans: Allah does not take knowledge away by pulling it out of people. He takes knowledge by taking the scholars, until when He has left no scholar behind,
story: It ends: people take ignorant men as leaders, and they are asked, and they answer without knowledge, and they go astray and lead others astray. Nothing is removed from anyone's head. People simply die and are not replaced.
arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَقْبِضُ الْعِلْمَ انْتِزَاعًا، يَنْتَزِعُهُ مِنَ الْعِبَادِ، وَلَكِنْ يَقْبِضُ الْعِلْمَ بِقَبْضِ الْعُلَمَاءِ، حَتَّى إِذَا لَمْ يُبْقِ عَالِمًا
english_full: Narrated `Abdullah bin `Amr bin Al-`As:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "Allah does not take away the knowledge, by taking it away from (the hearts of) the people, but takes it away by the death of the religious learned men till when none of the (religious learned men) remains, people will take as their leaders ignorant persons who when consulted will give their verdict without knowledge. So they will go astray and will lead the people astray

title: What he told the women who asked for a day
lede: One of them asked what happens with two.
translit: Mā minkunna-mraʾatun tuqaddimu thalāthatan min waladihā illā kāna lahā ḥijāban mina-n-nār
trans: There is not one of you who sends ahead three of her children but that they are a screen for her from the Fire.
story: The women had asked him to set aside a day for them, and he did. When he said it, a woman asked: and two? He said: and two.
arabic: مَا مِنْكُنَّ امْرَأَةٌ تُقَدِّمُ ثَلاَثَةً مِنْ وَلَدِهَا إِلاَّ كَانَ لَهَا حِجَابًا مِنَ النَّارِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri:Some women requested the Prophet (ﷺ) to fix a day for them as the men were taking all his time. On that he promised them one day for religious lessons and commandments. Once during such a lesson the Prophet said, "A woman whose three children die will be shielded by them from the Hell fire." On that a woman asked, "If only two die?" He replied, "Even two (will shield her from the Hell-fire)

title: What he said about the one who was killed
lede: They asked the obvious question about the second man.
translit: Idhā-ltaqā-l-muslimāni bi-sayfayhimā fa-l-qātilu wa-l-maqtūlu fi-n-nār
trans: When two Muslims meet with their swords, the killer and the killed are both in the Fire.
story: They said: this is the killer, but what about the one who was killed. He said: he was intent on killing his companion. What is being judged is what was in the hand and the intention behind it, not who happened to be faster.
arabic: إِذَا الْتَقَى الْمُسْلِمَانِ بِسَيْفَيْهِمَا فَالْقَاتِلُ وَالْمَقْتُولُ فِي النَّارِ
english_full: Narrated Al-Ahnaf bin Qais: While I was going to help this man ('Ali Ibn Abi Talib), Abu Bakra met me and asked, "Where are you going?" I replied, "I am going to help that person." He said, "Go back for I have heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, 'When two Muslims fight (meet) each other with their swords, both the murderer as well as the murdered will go to the Hell-fire.' I said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! It is all right for the murderer but what about the murdered one?' Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, "He surely had the intention to kill his companion

title: A time when the best thing to own is sheep
lede: It describes a man going uphill on purpose.
translit: Yūshiku an yakūna khayra māli-l-muslimi ghanamun yatbaʿu bihā shaʿafa-l-jibāli wa mawāqiʿa-l-qaṭr, yafirru bi-dīnihi mina-l-fitan
trans: It is close to the time when the best property a Muslim has will be sheep, which he follows to the mountain tops and the places where rain falls, fleeing with his religion from the trials.
story: The word used is fleeing, and what he is carrying out is his religion. It describes withdrawal as a legitimate move when staying costs more than it is worth.
arabic: يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَكُونَ خَيْرَ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِ غَنَمٌ يَتْبَعُ بِهَا شَعَفَ الْجِبَالِ وَمَوَاقِعَ الْقَطْرِ، يَفِرُّ بِدِينِهِ مِنَ الْفِتَنِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Said Al-Khudri: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "A time will soon come when the best property of a Muslim will be sheep which he will take on the top of mountains and the places of rainfall (valleys) so as to flee with his religion from afflictions

title: Three people who get paid twice
lede: Each of them had two claims to satisfy.
translit: Thalāthatun lahum ajrān: rajulun min ahli-l-kitābi āmana bi-nabiyyihi wa āmana bi-Muḥammad, wa-l-ʿabdu-l-mamlūku idhā addā ḥaqqa-Llāhi wa ḥaqqa mawālīh
trans: Three have two rewards: a man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in Muhammad, and an owned servant who fulfils the right of Allah and the right of those over him.
story: The third is a man who had a slave woman, taught her well, disciplined her well, freed her and then married her. In every case the doubling is for carrying two obligations at once rather than for doing anything extra.
arabic: ثَلاَثَةٌ لَهُمْ أَجْرَانِ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ آمَنَ بِنَبِيِّهِ، وَآمَنَ بِمُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَالْعَبْدُ الْمَمْلُوكُ إِذَا أَدَّى حَقَّ اللَّهِ وَحَقَّ مَوَالِيهِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Burda's father: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said "Three persons will have a double reward: 1. A Person from the people of the scriptures who believed in his prophet (Jesus or Moses) and then believed in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) (i.e. has embraced Islam). 2. A slave who discharges his duties to Allah and his master. 3. A master of a woman-slave who teaches her good manners and educates her in the best possible way (the religion) and manumits her and then marries her

title: What to do with something you find
lede: The instruction begins with looking at it closely.
translit: Iʿrif wikāʾahā wa ʿifāṣahā, thumma ʿarrifhā sanah, thumma-stamtiʿ bihā, fa-in jāʾa rabbuhā fa-addihā ilayh
trans: Note its tie and its container. Then announce it for a year. Then make use of it. And if its owner comes, hand it over to him.
story: A man asked what to do about picked up property. The whole year of announcing is so that the description can be checked when someone claims it, and the last clause has no time limit attached.
arabic: اعْرِفْ وِكَاءَهَا ـ أَوْ قَالَ وِعَاءَهَا ـ وَعِفَاصَهَا، ثُمَّ عَرِّفْهَا سَنَةً، ثُمَّ اسْتَمْتِعْ بِهَا، فَإِنْ جَاءَ رَبُّهَا فَأَدِّهَا إِلَيْهِ
english_full: Narrated Zaid bin Khalid Al-Juhani:A man asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the picking up of a "Luqata" (fallen lost thing). The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "Recognize and remember its tying material and its container, and make public announcement (about it) for one year, then utilize it but give it to its owner if he comes." Then the person asked about the lost camel. On that, the Prophet (ﷺ) got angry and his cheeks or his Face became red and he said, "You have no concern with it as it has its water container, and its feet and it will reach water, and eat (the leaves) of trees till its owner finds it." The man then asked about the lost sheep. The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "It is either for you, for your brother (another person) or for the wolf

title: Two conditions on the same promise
lede: Both of them are about why, not how much.
translit: Man yaqum laylata-l-qadri īmānan wa-ḥtisāban ghufira lahu mā taqaddama min dhanbih
trans: Whoever stands the Night of Decree out of faith and seeking the reward is forgiven what has gone before of his sin.
story: The same two conditions attach to fasting Ramadan and to standing its nights. Neither one specifies a length. Both specify a reason.
arabic: مَنْ يَقُمْ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever establishes the prayers on the night of Qadr out of sincere faith and hoping to attain Allah's rewards (not to show off) then all his past sins will be forgiven

title: What was guaranteed for the one who leaves
lede: Two outcomes and both of them are settled in advance.
translit: Intadaba-Llāhu li-man kharaja fī sabīlih, lā yukhrijuhu illā īmānun bī wa taṣdīqun bi-rusulī, an urjiʿahu bimā nāla min ajrin aw ghanīmah
trans: Allah has undertaken for the one who goes out in His path, driven out by nothing but faith in Me and belief in My messengers, that He will return him with whatever he gained of reward or spoils,
story: Or that He will admit him to the Garden. The clause in the middle is the qualifier: driven out by nothing but. It rules out every other reason a person might have had for going.
arabic: انْتَدَبَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ خَرَجَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ لاَ يُخْرِجُهُ إِلاَّ إِيمَانٌ بِي وَتَصْدِيقٌ بِرُسُلِي أَنْ أُرْجِعَهُ بِمَا نَالَ مِنْ أَجْرٍ أَوْ غَنِيمَةٍ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The person who participates in (Holy battles) in Allah's cause and nothing compels him to do so except belief in Allah and His Apostles, will be recompensed by Allah either with a reward, or booty (if he survives) or will be admitted to Paradise (if he is killed in the battle as a martyr). Had I not found it difficult for my followers, then I would not remain behind any sariya going for Jihad and I would have loved to be martyred in Allah's cause and then made alive, and then martyred and then made alive, and then again martyred in His cause

title: What happens to what came before
lede: It applies from the point the person gets it right.
translit: Idhā aslama-l-ʿabdu fa-ḥasuna islāmuh, yukaffiru-Llāhu ʿanhu kulla sayyiʾatin kāna zalafahā
trans: When a servant accepts Islam and makes his Islam good, Allah wipes out from him every bad deed he had put forward before.
story: Then the reckoning starts from there, with the good counted ten to seven hundred times and the bad counted once, unless Allah passes over it.
arabic: إِذَا أَسْلَمَ الْعَبْدُ فَحَسُنَ إِسْلاَمُهُ يُكَفِّرُ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ كُلَّ سَيِّئَةٍ كَانَ زَلَفَهَا
english_full: Narrated Abu Sa'id Al Khudri:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If a person embraces Islam sincerely, then Allah shall forgive all his past sins, and after that starts the settlement of accounts, the reward of his good deeds will be ten times to seven hundred times for each good deed and one evil deed will be recorded as it is unless Allah forgives it

title: Why he sent back a gift after one prayer
lede: He had prayed in it once and that was enough.
translit: Idhhabū bi-khamīṣatī hādhihi ilā Abī Jahm, wa-ʾtūnī bi-anbijāniyyati Abī Jahm, fa-innahā alhatnī ānifan ʿan ṣalātī
trans: Take this patterned cloak of mine to Abu Jahm and bring me Abu Jahm's plain one, for it just now distracted me from my prayer.
story: Abu Jahm had given him a cloak with markings on it. He prayed in it, looked at the patterns, and afterwards sent it straight back and asked for the coarse plain one instead.
arabic: اذْهَبُوا بِخَمِيصَتِي هَذِهِ إِلَى أَبِي جَهْمٍ وَائْتُونِي بِأَنْبِجَانِيَّةِ أَبِي جَهْمٍ، فَإِنَّهَا أَلْهَتْنِي آنِفًا عَنْ صَلاَتِي
english_full: Narrated `Aisha:the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed in a Khamisa (a square garment) having marks. During the prayer, he looked at its marks. So when he finished the prayer he said, "Take this Khamisa of mine to Abu Jahm and get me his Inbijaniya (a woolen garment without marks) as it (the Khamisa) has diverted my attention from the prayer." Narrated `Aisha: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'I was looking at its (Khamisa's) marks during the prayers and I was afraid that it may put me in trial (by taking away my attention)

title: What he said after praying the wrong number
lede: They asked whether something in the prayer had changed.
translit: Innahu law ḥadatha fi-ṣ-ṣalāti shayʾun la-nabbaʾtukum bih. Wa lākin innamā anā basharun mithlukum, ansā kamā tansawn, fa-idhā nasītu fa-dhakkirūnī
trans: If anything had changed in the prayer I would have told you. But I am only a human being like you. I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me.
story: He had prayed five and they mentioned it. He asked what it was, they told him, and he turned and made two prostrations. Then he said this.
arabic: إِنَّهُ لَوْ حَدَثَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ شَىْءٌ لَنَبَّأْتُكُمْ بِهِ، وَلَكِنْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ، أَنْسَى كَمَا تَنْسَوْنَ، فَإِذَا نَسِيتُ فَذَكِّرُونِي
english_full: Narrated `Abdullah:The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed (and the sub-narrator Ibrahim said, "I do not know whether he prayed more or less than usual"), and when he had finished the prayers he was asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Has there been any change in the prayers?" He said, "What is it?' The people said, "You have prayed so much and so much." So the Prophet (ﷺ) bent his legs, faced the Qibla and performed two prostration's (of Sahu) and finished his prayers with Taslim (by turning his face to right and left saying: 'As-Salamu `Alaikum- Warahmat-ullah'). When he turned his face to us he said, "If there had been anything changed in the prayer, surely I would have informed you but I am a human being like you and liable to forget like you. So if I forget remind me and if anyone of you is doubtful about his prayer, he should follow what he thinks to be correct and complete his prayer accordingly and finish it and do two prostrations (of Sahu)

title: What is actually happening while a person stands there
lede: It is given as the reason for a rule about spitting.
translit: Inna aḥadakum idhā qāma fī ṣalātihi fa-innahu yunājī rabbah
trans: When one of you stands in his prayer, he is in intimate conversation with his Lord.
story: Munājāh is the word for speaking quietly to someone close enough to hear it. It is not used here as encouragement. It is used as the explanation for why you would not turn your face aside and spit while you are doing it.
arabic: إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ إِذَا قَامَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ يُنَاجِي رَبَّهُ
english_full: Narrated Anas bin Malik:The Prophet (ﷺ) saw some sputum in the direction of the Qibla (on the wall of the mosque) and he disliked that and the sign of disgust was apparent from his face. So he got up and scraped it off with his hand and said, "Whenever anyone of you stands for the prayer, he is speaking in private to his Lord or his Lord is between him and his Qibla. So, none of you should spit in the direction of the Qibla but one can spit to the left or under his foot." The Prophet (ﷺ) then took the corner of his sheet and spat in it and folded it and said, "Or you can do this

title: What he told them he could see
lede: He asked them a question before saying it.
translit: Hal tarawna qiblatī hāhunā. Fa-wa-Llāhi mā yakhfā ʿalayya khushūʿukum wa lā rukūʿukum, innī la-arākum min warāʾi ẓahrī
trans: Do you think my face is only towards here? By Allah, neither your stillness nor your bowing is hidden from me. I see you from behind my back.
arabic: هَلْ تَرَوْنَ قِبْلَتِي هَا هُنَا فَوَاللَّهِ مَا يَخْفَى عَلَىَّ خُشُوعُكُمْ وَلاَ رُكُوعُكُمْ، إِنِّي لأَرَاكُمْ مِنْ وَرَاءِ ظَهْرِي
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Do you consider or see that my face is towards the Qibla? By Allah, neither your submissiveness nor your bowing is hidden from me, surely I see you from my back

title: What he said passing the ruins
lede: He covered his head and hurried the animal through.
translit: Lā tadkhulū ʿalā hāʾulāʾi-l-muʿadhdhabīna illā an takūnū bākīn. Fa-in lam takūnū bākīna fa-lā tadkhulū ʿalayhim, lā yuṣībukum mā aṣābahum
trans: Do not go in among these people who were punished unless you are weeping. And if you are not weeping, do not go in among them, so that what struck them does not strike you.
story: They were passing the dwellings of Thamud. The instruction is not to avoid the place. It is about what you are feeling when you look at it, and treating other people's ruin as a spectacle is the thing named as dangerous.
arabic: لاَ تَدْخُلُوا عَلَى هَؤُلاَءِ الْمُعَذَّبِينَ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونُوا بَاكِينَ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بَاكِينَ فَلاَ تَدْخُلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ، لاَ يُصِيبُكُمْ مَا أَصَابَهُمْ
english_full: Narrated `Abdullah bin `Umar:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Do not enter (the places) of these people where Allah's punishment had fallen unless you do so weeping. If you do not weep, do not enter (the places of these people) because Allah's curse and punishment which fell upon them may fall upon you

title: What is built in return
lede: One condition is attached and it is not about the size.
translit: Man banā masjidan lillāhi ka-mafḥaṣi qaṭātin aw aṣghar, bana-Llāhu lahu baytan fi-l-jannah
trans: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, even the size of a sandgrouse's scrape in the ground or smaller, Allah builds him a house in the Garden.
story: A sandgrouse makes its nest by scratching a shallow dip in the ground. It is the smallest structure the desert offered as a comparison, and the return on it is a house.
arabic: مَنْ بَنَى مَسْجِدًا لِلَّهِ كَمَفْحَصِ قَطَاةٍ أَوْ أَصْغَرَ بَنَى اللَّهُ لَهُ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ
english_full: It was narrated from Jabir bin 'Abdullah that:The Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever builds a mosque for the sake of Allah, like a sparrow's nest for Allah or even smaller, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise

title: What to do carrying something sharp through a crowd
lede: A small rule with the reason attached.
translit: Man marra fī shayʾin min masājidinā aw aswāqinā bi-nabl, fa-lyaʾkhudh ʿalā niṣālihā, lā yaʿqir bi-kaffihi musliman
trans: Whoever passes through any of our mosques or markets carrying arrows should hold them by their heads, so that he does not wound a Muslim with his hand.
story: It is not about weapons. It is about what your hand is doing in a crowded place, and it puts the burden on the person carrying rather than on everyone else to get out of the way.
arabic: مَنْ مَرَّ فِي شَىْءٍ مِنْ مَسَاجِدِنَا أَوْ أَسْوَاقِنَا بِنَبْلٍ، فَلْيَأْخُذْ عَلَى نِصَالِهَا، لاَ يَعْقِرْ بِكَفِّهِ مُسْلِمًا
english_full: Narrated Abu Burda bin `Abdullah:(on the authority of his father) The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever passes through our mosques or markets with arrows should hold them by their heads lest he should injure a Muslim

title: What he said about a hundred conditions
lede: Someone had tried to attach terms to a sale.
translit: Mā bālu aqwāmin yashtariṭūna shurūṭan laysat fī kitābi-Llāh. Mani-shtaraṭa sharṭan laysa fī kitābi-Llāhi fa-laysa lah, wa ini-shtaraṭa miʾata marrah
trans: What is the matter with people who stipulate conditions that are not in the Book of Allah? Whoever stipulates a condition that is not in the Book of Allah does not have it, even if he stipulates it a hundred times.
story: Aisha had wanted to buy Barirah and free her, and her owners wanted to keep the right of inheritance. Repeating a condition does not make it stronger, and the number is named to make the point.
arabic: مَا بَالُ أَقْوَامٍ يَشْتَرِطُونَ شُرُوطًا لَيْسَتْ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ، مَنِ اشْتَرَطَ شَرْطًا لَيْسَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ لَهُ، وَإِنِ اشْتَرَطَ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ
english_full: Narrated `Aisha:Barirah came to seek my help regarding her manumission (freedom). I told her, "If you like I would pay your price to your masters but your Wala' (allegiance) would be for me." Her masters said, "If you like, you can pay what remains (of the price of her manumission), (Sufyan the sub-narrator once said), or if you like you can manumit her, but her (inheritance) Al-Wala would be for us. "When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came, I spoke to him about it. He said, "Buy her and manumit her. No doubt Al-Wala' is for the manumitted." Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stood on the pulpit (or Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit as Sufyan once said), and said, "What about some people who impose conditions which are not present in Allah's Book (Laws)? Whoever imposes conditions which are not in Allah's Book (Laws), his conditions will be invalid even if he imposed them a hundred times

title: What he announced from the pulpit, and who understood it
lede: Only one man in the mosque started crying.
translit: Inna-Llāha khayyara ʿabdan bayna-d-dunyā wa bayna mā ʿindah, fa-khtāra mā ʿinda-Llāh
trans: Allah gave a servant the choice between this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Allah.
story: Abu Bakr wept. The others wondered why an old man would cry over a servant being given a choice. He was the one who had understood that the servant was the Prophet, and that he was telling them he was going.
arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَيَّرَ عَبْدًا بَيْنَ الدُّنْيَا وَبَيْنَ مَا عِنْدَهُ، فَاخْتَارَ مَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri:The Prophet (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said, "Allah gave a choice to one of (His) slaves either to choose this world or what is with Him in the Hereafter. He chose the latter." Abu Bakr wept. I said to myself, "Why is this Sheikh weeping, if Allah gave choice to one (of His) slaves either to choose this world or what is with Him in the Here after and he chose the latter?" And that slave was Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) himself. Abu Bakr knew more than us. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "O Abu Bakr! Don't weep. The Prophet (ﷺ) added: Abu- Bakr has favored me much with his property and company. If I were to take a Khalil from mankind I would certainly have taken Abu Bakr but the Islamic brotherhood and friendship is sufficient. Close all the gates in the mosque except that of Abu Bakr

title: What he said about Abu Bakr in the same sermon
lede: He named the one exception and then closed it off.
translit: Innahu laysa mina-n-nāsi aḥadun amanna ʿalayya fī nafsihi wa mālihi min Abī Bakri-bni Abī Quḥāfah
trans: There is no one among people who has been more generous to me with himself and his wealth than Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah.
story: He went on: and if I were to take a bosom friend from among people I would have taken Abu Bakr. But the brotherhood of Islam and its affection is enough. Then he ordered every door onto the mosque closed except Abu Bakr's.
arabic: إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنَ النَّاسِ أَحَدٌ أَمَنَّ عَلَىَّ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَمَالِهِ مِنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي قُحَافَةَ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:"Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) in his fatal illness came out with a piece of cloth tied round his head and sat on the pulpit. After thanking and praising Allah he said, "There is no one who had done more favor to me with life and property than Abu Bakr bin Abi Quhafa. If I were to take a Khalil, I would certainly have taken Abu- Bakr but the Islamic brotherhood is superior. Close all the small doors in this mosque except that of Abu Bakr

title: What he answered when asked about the night prayer
lede: A man called out the question from the back.
translit: Mathnā mathnā. Fa-idhā khashīta-ṣ-ṣubḥa fa-awtir bi-wāḥidah, tūtiru laka mā qad ṣallayt
trans: Two by two. And when you fear the dawn, make it odd with one, which makes odd for you all that you have prayed.
story: No total is given. You pray in pairs for as long as you have, and the single unit at the end is what closes whatever amount you managed.
arabic: مَثْنَى مَثْنَى، فَإِذَا خَشِيتَ الصُّبْحَ فَأَوْتِرْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ، تُوتِرُ لَكَ مَا قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Umar:A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was delivering the sermon and asked him how to offer the night prayers. The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, 'Pray two rak`at at a time and then two and then two and so on and if you are afraid of dawn (the approach of the time of the Fajr prayer) pray one rak`a and that will be the witr for all the rak`at which you have prayed." Narrated 'Ubaidullah bin `Abdullah bin `Umar: A man called the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the mosque

title: What passing in front of someone praying costs
lede: The unit is left unstated on purpose.
translit: Law yaʿlamu-l-mārru bayna yaday-l-muṣallī mādhā ʿalayhi la-kāna an yaqifa arbaʿīna khayran lahu min an yamurra bayna yadayh
trans: If the one who passes in front of a person praying knew what it costs him, standing still for forty would be better for him than passing in front of him.
story: The narrator says he does not know whether he said forty days, or months, or years. He left it as a number with no unit, and the point survives either way.
arabic: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الْمَارُّ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْمُصَلِّي مَاذَا عَلَيْهِ لَكَانَ أَنْ يَقِفَ أَرْبَعِينَ خَيْرًا لَهُ مِنْ أَنْ يَمُرَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
english_full: Narrated Busr bin Sa`id:that Zaid bin Khalid sent him to Abi Juhaim to ask him what he had heard from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) about a person passing in front of another person who was praying. Abu Juhaim replied, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'If the person who passes in front of another person in prayer knew the magnitude of his sin he would prefer to wait for 40 (days, months or years) rather than to pass in front of him." Abu An-Nadr said, "I do not remember exactly whether he said 40 days, months or years

title: What he sent as a message to a delegation
lede: He told them to carry it back to whoever was behind them.
translit: Āmurukum bi-arbaʿ, wa anhākum ʿan arbaʿ: al-īmāni bi-Llāh
trans: I command you four things, and I forbid you four. Faith in Allah.
story: The delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays said they could only reach him in the sacred month and asked for something decisive they could carry home. He gave them belief, then explained it as the testimony, the prayer, the zakat, and giving a fifth of what they gained. Then he named four vessels they were to avoid.
arabic: آمُرُكُمْ بِأَرْبَعٍ، وَأَنْهَاكُمْ عَنْ أَرْبَعٍ الإِيمَانِ بِاللَّهِ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:"Once a delegation of `Abdul Qais came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "We belong to such and such branch of the tribe of Rabi'ah and we can only come to you in the sacred months. Order us to do something good so that we may take it from you and also invite to it those whom we have left behind (at home)." So he said, "I order you to do four things and forbid you from four things: To believe in Allah" - and then he explained it to them "to testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and that I am Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), to establish the prayers (at the stated times), to pay the Zakat (obligatory charity), to hand me the Khumus (fifth) if you acquire spoils of war. And I forbid from (using) Dubba, Hantam, Muqaiyyar, and Naqir (all these were utensils used for the preparation of alcoholic drinks)

title: What the ordinary acts wipe out
lede: Hudhayfah was asked who remembered him saying it.
translit: Fitnatu-r-rajuli fī ahlihi wa mālihi wa waladihi wa jārihi tukaffiruhā-ṣ-ṣalātu wa-ṣ-ṣawmu wa-ṣ-ṣadaqatu wa-l-amru wa-n-nahy
trans: A man's trial in his family, his wealth, his child and his neighbour is wiped out by the prayer, the fasting, the charity, and enjoining good and forbidding wrong.
story: Umar asked who had memorised it. Hudhayfah said he had, and Umar said: you are bold. The four things named as trials are the four things a person is most attached to, and none of them are removed. They are covered over.
arabic: فِتْنَةُ الرَّجُلِ فِي أَهْلِهِ وَمَالِهِ وَوَلَدِهِ وَجَارِهِ تُكَفِّرُهَا الصَّلاَةُ وَالصَّوْمُ وَالصَّدَقَةُ وَالأَمْرُ وَالنَّهْىُ
english_full: Narrated Shaqiq:that he had heard Hudhaifa saying, "Once I was sitting with `Umar and he said, 'Who amongst you remembers the statement of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) about the afflictions?' I said, 'I know it as the Prophet (ﷺ) had said it.' `Umar said, 'No doubt you are bold.' I said, 'The afflictions caused for a man by his wife, money, children and neighbor are expiated by his prayers, fasting, charity and by enjoining (what is good) and forbidding (what is evil).' `Umar said, 'I did not mean that but I asked about that affliction which will spread like the waves of the sea.' I (Hudhaifa) said, 'O leader of the faithful believers! You need not be afraid of it as there is a closed door between you and it.' `Umar asked, Will the door be broken or opened?' I replied, 'It will be broken.' `Umar said, 'Then it will never be closed again.' I was asked whether `Umar knew that door. I replied that he knew it as one knows that there will be night before the tomorrow morning. I narrated a Hadith that was free from any misstatement" The subnarrator added that they deputized Masruq to ask Hudhaifa (about the door). Hudhaifa said, "The door was `Umar himself

title: A question he asked instead of a statement
lede: He waited for them to answer it themselves.
translit: A-raʾaytum law anna naharan bi-bābi aḥadikum yaghtasilu fīhi kulla yawmin khamsan, mā taqūlu dhālika yubqī min daranih
trans: Tell me, if there were a river at the door of one of you and he washed in it five times a day, would that leave any of his dirt behind?
story: They said: it would not leave any dirt at all. He said: that is the likeness of the five prayers. Allah wipes out wrong actions with them.
arabic: أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ أَنَّ نَهَرًا بِبَابِ أَحَدِكُمْ، يَغْتَسِلُ فِيهِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ خَمْسًا، مَا تَقُولُ ذَلِكَ يُبْقِي مِنْ دَرَنِهِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "If there was a river at the door of anyone of you and he took a bath in it five times a day would you notice any dirt on him?" They said, "Not a trace of dirt would be left." The Prophet (ﷺ) added, "That is the example of the five prayers with which Allah blots out (annuls) evil deeds

title: The one time he opened the floor completely
lede: People began asking, and it was not a comfortable session.
translit: Man aḥabba an yasʾala ʿan shayʾin fa-lyasʾal. Fa-lā tasʾalūnī ʿan shayʾin illā akhbartukum mā dumtu fī maqāmī hādhā
trans: Whoever wants to ask about anything, let him ask. You will not ask me about anything without my telling you, as long as I am standing in this place of mine.
story: Anas says the people wept a great deal that day, and he kept saying: ask me. A man stood and asked where he would end up and was told: the Fire. Another asked who his father was and was told a name he had not been claiming.
arabic: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ عَنْ شَىْءٍ فَلْيَسْأَلْ، فَلاَ تَسْأَلُونِي عَنْ شَىْءٍ إِلاَّ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ مَا دُمْتُ فِي مَقَامِي هَذَا
english_full: Narrated Anas bin Malik:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came out as the sun declined at midday and offered the Zuhr prayer. He then stood on the pulpit and spoke about the Hour (Day of Judgment) and said that in it there would be tremendous things. He then said, "Whoever likes to ask me about anything he can do so and I shall reply as long as I am at this place of mine. Most of the people wept and the Prophet (ﷺ) said repeatedly, "Ask me." `Abdullah bin Hudhafa As-Sahmi stood up and said, "Who is my father?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Your father is Hudhafa." The Prophet (ﷺ) repeatedly said, "Ask me." Then `Umar knelt before him and said, "We are pleased with Allah as our Lord, Islam as our religion, and Muhammad as our Prophet." The Prophet then became quiet and said, "Paradise and Hell-fire were displayed in front of me on this wall just now and I have never seen a better thing (than the former) and a worse thing (than the latter)

title: Two shifts, and where they overlap
lede: They are asked a question when they go up.
translit: Yataʿāqabūna fīkum malāʾikatun bi-l-layli wa malāʾikatun bi-n-nahār, wa yajtamiʿūna fī ṣalāti-l-fajri wa ṣalāti-l-ʿaṣr
trans: Angels take turns among you, some by night and some by day, and they come together at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.
story: Then those who stayed the night go up, and He asks them, though He knows better, how they left His servants. They say: we left them praying, and we came to them while they were praying.
arabic: يَتَعَاقَبُونَ فِيكُمْ مَلاَئِكَةٌ بِاللَّيْلِ وَمَلاَئِكَةٌ بِالنَّهَارِ، وَيَجْتَمِعُونَ فِي صَلاَةِ الْفَجْرِ وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Angels come to you in succession by night and day and all of them get together at the time of the Fajr and `Asr prayers. Those who have passed the night with you (or stayed with you) ascend (to the Heaven) and Allah asks them, though He knows everything about you, well, "In what state did you leave my slaves?" The angels reply: "When we left them they were praying and when we reached them, they were praying

title: What he said to people who had waited a long time
lede: They had been sitting for the night prayer until nearly midnight.
translit: ʿAlā rislikum, abshirū. Inna min niʿmati-Llāhi ʿalaykum annahu laysa aḥadun mina-n-nāsi yuṣallī hādhihi-s-sāʿata ghayrukum
trans: Take it easy. Take the good news. It is part of Allah's favour on you that there is nobody among people praying at this hour except you.
story: He came out after they had waited, and the first thing he said was not an apology and not an instruction. He told them the waiting itself was the thing they had been given.
arabic: عَلَى رِسْلِكُمْ، أَبْشِرُوا إِنَّ مِنْ نِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ يُصَلِّي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةَ غَيْرُكُمْ
english_full: Narrated Abu Musa:My companions, who came with me in the boat and I landed at a place called Baqi [??] Buthan [??] . The Prophet (ﷺ) was in Medina at that time. One of us used to go to the Prophet (ﷺ) by turns every night at the time of the `Isha prayer. Once I along with my companions went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he was busy in some of his affairs, so the `Isha' prayer was delayed to the middle of the night He then came out and led the people (in prayer). After finishing from the prayer, he addressed the people present there saying, "Be patient! Don't go away. Have the glad tiding. It is from the blessing of Allah upon you that none amongst mankind has prayed at this time save you." Or said, "None except you has prayed at this time." Abu Musa added, 'So we returned happily after what we heard from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)

title: What counts as having caught the prayer
lede: It is set at a single unit at either end of the day.
translit: Man adraka mina-ṣ-ṣubḥi rakʿatan qabla an taṭluʿa-sh-shamsu fa-qad adraka-ṣ-ṣubḥ
trans: Whoever catches one unit of the dawn prayer before the sun rises has caught the dawn prayer.
story: And whoever catches one unit of the afternoon prayer before the sun sets has caught the afternoon prayer. Almost missing it and missing it are treated as different things.
arabic: مَنْ أَدْرَكَ مِنَ الصُّبْحِ رَكْعَةً قَبْلَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ الصُّبْحَ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever could get one rak`a (of the Fajr prayer) before sunrise, he has got the (morning) prayer and whoever could get one rak`a of the `Asr prayer before sunset, he has got the (`Asr) prayer

title: What is owed to a person once they pray with you
lede: Three ordinary things, and then a warning.
translit: Man ṣallā ṣalātanā wa-staqbala qiblatanā wa akala dhabīḥatanā, fa-dhālika-l-muslimu-lladhī lahu dhimmatu-Llāhi wa dhimmatu rasūlih, fa-lā tukhfirū-Llāh
trans: Whoever prays our prayer, faces our direction and eats what we slaughter, that is the Muslim who has the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger. So do not betray Allah in what He has guaranteed.
story: The test is entirely external and any observer can apply it. And what follows from passing it is not acceptance but a guarantee, which is described as belonging to Allah rather than to the community.
arabic: مَنْ صَلَّى صَلاَتَنَا، وَاسْتَقْبَلَ قِبْلَتَنَا، وَأَكَلَ ذَبِيحَتَنَا، فَذَلِكَ الْمُسْلِمُ الَّذِي لَهُ ذِمَّةُ اللَّهِ وَذِمَّةُ رَسُولِهِ، فَلاَ تُخْفِرُوا اللَّهَ
english_full: Narrated Anas bin Malik:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever prays like us and faces our Qibla and eats our slaughtered animals is a Muslim and is under Allah's and His Apostle's protection. So do not betray Allah by betraying those who are in His protection

title: What he answered when a woman had nothing to wear
lede: They had asked whether she should stay home.
translit: Li-tulbis-hā ṣāḥibatuhā min jilbābihā, wa li-tashhadi-l-khayra wa daʿwata-l-muslimīn
trans: Let her companion lend her part of her own outer garment, and let her be present for the good and the supplication of the Muslims.
story: He had ordered the women out for the two festivals, including those who were excused from praying. Umm ʿAtiyyah says they said: one of us has no outer garment. The answer was not that she should stay behind.
arabic: لِتُلْبِسْهَا صَاحِبَتُهَا مِنْ جِلْبَابِهَا، وَلْتَشْهَدِ الْخَيْرَ وَدَعْوَةَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
english_full: Narrated Aiyub:Hafsa said, 'We used to forbid our young women to go out for the two `Id prayers. A woman came and stayed at the palace of Bani Khalaf and she narrated about her sister whose husband took part in twelve holy battles along with the Prophet (ﷺ) and her sister was with her husband in six (out of these twelve). She (the woman's sister) said, "We used to treat the wounded, look after the patients and once I asked the Prophet, 'Is there any harm for any of us to stay at home if she doesn't have a veil?' He said, 'She should cover herself with the veil of her companion and should participate in the good deeds and in the religious gathering of the Muslims.' When Um `Atiya came I asked her whether she had heard it from the Prophet. She replied, "Yes. May my father be sacrificed for him (the Prophet)! (Whenever she mentioned the Prophet (ﷺ) she used to say, 'May my father be sacrificed for him) I have heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying, 'The unmarried young virgins and the mature girl who stay often screened or the young unmarried virgins who often stay screened and the menstruating women should come out and participate in the good deeds as well as the religious gathering of the faithful believers but the menstruating women should keep away from the Musalla (praying place).' " Hafsa asked Um `Atiya surprisingly, "Do you say the menstruating women?" She replied, "Doesn't a menstruating woman attend `Arafat (Hajj) and such and such (other deeds)?

title: How the prayer was first given
lede: One of the two was left as it was.
translit: Faraḍa-Llāhu-ṣ-ṣalāta ḥīna faraḍahā rakʿatayni rakʿatayni fi-l-ḥaḍari wa-s-safar, fa-uqirrat ṣalātu-s-safar, wa zīda fī ṣalāti-l-ḥaḍar
trans: When Allah made the prayer obligatory He made it two units and two units, at home and on a journey. Then the travelling prayer was left as it was, and the prayer at home was increased.
story: Aisha reports it. The shortened prayer on a journey is not a reduction from the full one. It is the original, and the longer one is the addition.
arabic: فَرَضَ اللَّهُ الصَّلاَةَ حِينَ فَرَضَهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي الْحَضَرِ وَالسَّفَرِ، فَأُقِرَّتْ صَلاَةُ السَّفَرِ، وَزِيدَ فِي صَلاَةِ الْحَضَرِ
english_full: Narrated `Aisha:the mother of believers: Allah enjoined the prayer and when He enjoined it, it was two rak`at only (in every prayer) both when in residence or on journey. Then the prayers offered on journey remained the same, but (the rak`at of) the prayers for non-travelers were increased

title: What he said while they were carrying bricks
lede: ʿAmmar was helping build the mosque when it was said.
translit: Wayḥa ʿAmmār, taqtuluhu-l-fiʾatu-l-bāghiyah, yadʿūhum ilā-l-jannah wa yadʿūnahu ilā-n-nār
trans: Alas for ʿAmmar. The transgressing party will kill him. He calls them to the Garden and they call him to the Fire.
story: ʿAmmar was carrying two bricks for every one the others carried. He was killed decades later, and the companions who were present recognised the words when it happened.
arabic: وَيْحَ عَمَّارٍ تَقْتُلُهُ الْفِئَةُ الْبَاغِيَةُ، يَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَيَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى النَّارِ
english_full: Narrated `Ikrima:Ibn `Abbas said to me and to his son `Ali, "Go to Abu Sa`id and listen to what he narrates." So we went and found him in a garden looking after it. He picked up his Rida', wore it and sat down and started narrating till the topic of the construction of the mosque reached. He said, "We were carrying one adobe at a time while `Ammar was carrying two. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw him and started removing the dust from his body and said, "May Allah be Merciful to `Ammar. He will be inviting them (i.e. his murderers, the rebellious group) to Paradise and they will invite him to Hell-fire." `Ammar said, "I seek refuge with Allah from affliction

title: What he said one evening after the night prayer
lede: It caused a misunderstanding that had to be corrected.
translit: A-raʾaytum laylatakum hādhih, fa-inna raʾsa miʾati sanatin minhā lā yabqā mimman huwa ʿalā ẓahri-l-arḍi aḥad
trans: Do you see this night of yours? At the end of a hundred years from it, no one now on the face of the earth will be left.
story: Ibn Umar says people misunderstood it as a statement about the world ending. What he meant was that this particular generation would be gone.
arabic: أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَيْلَتَكُمْ هَذِهِ فَإِنَّ رَأْسَ مِائَةِ سَنَةٍ مِنْهَا لاَ يَبْقَى مِمَّنْ هُوَ عَلَى ظَهْرِ الأَرْضِ أَحَدٌ
english_full: Narrated `Abdullah:"One night Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) led us in the `Isha' prayer and that is the one called Al-`Atma [??] by the people. After the completion of the prayer, he faced us and said, "Do you know the importance of this night? Nobody present on the surface of the earth tonight will be living after one hundred years from this night." (See Hadith No)

title: The one he called the chief way of asking
lede: Said once at either end of the day, with a promise attached.
translit: Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa anā ʿabduk, wa anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika mā-staṭaʿt. Aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt. Abūʾu bi-niʿmatika wa abūʾu bi-dhanbī fa-ghfir lī, innahu lā yaghfiru-dh-dhunūba illā ant
trans: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I am on Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour to me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me. None forgives sins but You.
story: Whoever says it in the morning or the evening and dies that day or that night enters the Garden. The clause in the middle is the honest one: as much as I am able. It does not claim the covenant was kept.
note: Known as sayyid al-istighfār, the chief of the ways of asking forgiveness.

gradings: Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid: Sahih

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ أَبُوءُ بِنِعْمَتِكَ وَأَبُوءُ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي إِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ
english_full: Narrated Buraydah ibn al-Hasib: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: If anyone says in the morning or in the evening: "O Allah! Thou art my Lord; there is no god but Thee, Thou hast created me, and I am Thy servant and hold to Thy covenant and promise as much as I can; I seek refuge in Thee from the evil of what I have done: I acknowledge Thy favour to me, and I acknowledge my sin; pardon me, for none but Thee pardons sins, and dies during the daytime or during the night." he will go to Paradise

title: What he said watching a man's face go red
lede: Two men were insulting each other in front of him.
translit: Innī la-aʿlamu kalimatan law qālahā la-dhahaba ʿanhu mā yajid. Law qāla: aʿūdhu bi-Llāhi mina-sh-shayṭāni-r-rajīm
trans: I know a word which, if he said it, what he is feeling would leave him. If he said: I seek refuge in Allah from the rejected Satan.
story: They turned to the man and said: do you not hear what the Prophet is saying? He said: I am not mad. He was too far into it to take the way out, and it was said in front of him anyway.
arabic: إِنِّي لأَعْلَمُ كَلِمَةً لَوْ قَالَهَا لَذَهَبَ عَنْهُ مَا يَجِدُ لَوْ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
english_full: Narrated Sulaiman bin Sarad:Two men abused each other in front of the Prophet (ﷺ) while we were sitting with him. One of the two abused his companion furiously and his face became red. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I know a word (sentence) the saying of which will cause him to relax if this man says it. Only if he said, "I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the outcast.' " So they said to that (furious) man, 'Don't you hear what the Prophet (ﷺ) is saying?" He said, "I am not mad

title: The words he used over Hasan and Husayn
lede: He told them where the words came from.
translit: Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-Llāhi-t-tāmmati min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, wa min kulli ʿaynin lāmmah
trans: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every crawling thing, and from every eye that harms.
story: He would seek protection for Hasan and Husayn with it and say: your father used to seek protection with it for Ismaʿil and Ishaq. Three things named: what cannot be seen, what can be seen and bites, and what a person does with a look.
arabic: إِنَّ أَبَاكُمَا كَانَ يُعَوِّذُ بِهَا إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ، أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لاَمَّةٍ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek Refuge with Allah for Al-Hasan and Al-Husain and say: "Your forefather (i.e. Abraham) used to seek Refuge with Allah for Ishmael and Isaac by reciting the following: 'O Allah! I seek Refuge with Your Perfect Words from every devil and from poisonous pests and from every evil, harmful, envious eye

title: What Ibn Umar told a man to say lying down
lede: Someone asked whether he had it from Umar.
translit: Allāhumma khalaqta nafsī wa anta tawaffāhā, laka mamātuhā wa maḥyāhā. In aḥyaytahā fa-ḥfaẓhā, wa in amattahā fa-ghfir lahā. Allāhumma innī asʾaluka-l-ʿāfiyah
trans: O Allah, You created my soul and You take it. Its death and its life belong to You. If You keep it alive, guard it. If You cause it to die, forgive it. O Allah, I ask You for wellbeing.
story: A man asked him: did you hear this from Umar? He said: from someone better than Umar. From the Messenger of Allah.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ خَلَقْتَ نَفْسِي وَأَنْتَ تَوَفَّاهَا لَكَ مَمَاتُهَا وَمَحْيَاهَا إِنْ أَحْيَيْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا وَإِنْ أَمَتَّهَا فَاغْفِرْ لَهَا اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ
english_full: Abdullah b. 'Umar commanded a person that as he went to bed, he should say:" O Allah, Thou created my being and it is for Thee to take it to its ultimate goal. And its death and life is due to Thee, and if Thou givest it life, safeguard it; and if Thou bringst death, grant it pardon. O Allah, I beg of Thee safety." A person said to him: Did you hear it from Umar? Thereupon he said: (I have heard from one) who is better than Umar, viz. from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). Ibn Nafi, reported this on the authority of Abdullah b. Harith but he did not make mention of this" that he heard it himself

title: The single request he ranked above all others
lede: One word covers both places.
translit: Allāhumma innī asʾaluka-l-muʿāfāta fi-d-dunyā wa-l-ākhirah
trans: O Allah, I ask You for wellbeing in this world and the next.
story: There is no supplication a servant makes better than this one. Muʿāfāh is not health and it is not comfort. It is being let off, being kept clear of the thing rather than carried through it.
dissent: Scholars differ on this chain. Zubair Ali Zai grades it Daif. The majority (3 of 4) authenticate it.
arabic: مَا مِنْ دَعْوَةٍ يَدْعُو بِهَا الْعَبْدُ أَفْضَلَ مِنَ - اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْمُعَافَاةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ
english_full: It was narrated that Abu Hurairah said:"The Messenger of Allah (saas) said: 'There is no supplication that a person can say that is better than: Allahumma inni as'aluka al-mu'afah fid-dunya wal-akhirah (O Allah, I ask You for Al-Mu'afah in this world and in the Hereafter)

title: What to say after a bad dream
lede: Abdullah ibn Amr taught it to his children.
translit: Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti-Llāhi-t-tāmmati min ghaḍabihi wa ʿiqābihi wa sharri ʿibādihi, wa min hamazāti-sh-shayāṭīni wa an yaḥḍurūn
trans: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His anger and His punishment, from the evil of His servants, and from the promptings of the devils and that they should be present with me.
story: When one of you wakes in fright in the night, let him say it, and it will not harm him. Abdullah ibn Amr taught it to the children old enough to learn it, and for the ones too young he wrote it out and hung it on them.
dissent: Scholars differ on this chain. Zubair Ali Zai grades it Daif. The majority (3 of 4) authenticate it.
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ غَضَبِهِ وَعِقَابِهِ وَشَرِّ عِبَادِهِ وَمِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ
english_full: Amr bin Shu`aib narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:“When one of you becomes frightened during sleep, then let him say: ‘I seek refuge in Allah’s Perfect Words from His anger, His punishment, and the evil of His creatures, from the whisperings of the Shayatin, and that they should come (A`ūdhu bikalimātillāhit-tāmmati min ghaḍabihī wa `iqābihī wa sharri `ibādih, wa min hamazātish-shayāṭīni wa an yaḥḍurūn).’ For verily, they shall not harm him.” He said: “So `Abdullah bin `Amr used to teach it to those of his children who attained maturity, and those of them who did not, he would write it on a sheet and then hang it around his neck.”

title: What they heard him say in the middle of a prayer
lede: They saw him reach out for something that was not there.
translit: Aʿūdhu bi-Llāhi mink
trans: I seek refuge in Allah from you.
story: Abu ad-Darda says he stood to pray and they heard him say it, then curse three times, and stretch out his hand as though taking hold of something. Afterwards they asked. He said the enemy of Allah had come with a torch of fire to throw in his face, and that had he not remembered a prayer of Sulayman he would have tied him to a pillar of the mosque for the children of Madinah to play with.
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْكَ
english_full: Abu Darda' reported:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stood up (to pray) and we heard him say:" I seek refuge in Allah from thee." Then said:" curse thee with Allah's curse" three times, then he stretched out his hand as though he was taking hold of something. When he finished the prayer, we said: Messenger of Allah, we heard you say something during the prayer which we have not heard you say before, and we saw you stretch out your hand. He replied: Allah's enemy Iblis came with a flame of fire to put it in my face, so I said three times:" I Seek refuge in Allah from thee." Then I said three times:" I curse thee with Allah's full curse." But he did not retreat (on any one of these) three occasions. Thereafter I meant to seize him. I swear by Allah that had it not been for the supplication of my brother Sulaiman he would have been bound, and made an object of sport for the children of Medina

title: What to say over something newly yours
lede: It asks about what the thing already is, not what it will do.
translit: Allāhumma innī asʾaluka min khayrihā wa khayri mā jubilat ʿalayh, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharrihā wa sharri mā jubilat ʿalayh
trans: O Allah, I ask You for the good in her and the good of what she was made with, and I seek refuge in You from the evil in her and the evil of what she was made with.
story: He said: when one of you comes to have a wife, or someone who serves him, or a riding animal, let him take hold of the forelock and say it. Jubila ʿalayh is what a nature was formed on, before anybody chose anything.
note: Said over a marriage, and over anything else newly taken on.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِهَا وَخَيْرِ مَا جُبِلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا وَشَرِّ مَا جُبِلَتْ عَلَيْهِ
english_full: It was narrated from 'Abdullah bin 'Amr:that the Prophet said: “When anyone of you gets a new wife, a servant, or an animal, let him take hold of the forelock and say: Allahumma inni as`aluka min khayriha wa khayri ma jubilat 'alaihi, wa 'audhu bika min sharriha wa sharri ma jubilat `alaih (O Allah, I ask You for the goodness within her and the goodness that she is inclined towards, and I seek refuge with you from the evil to which she is inclined).' ”

title: Three things he asked to be spared on a journey
lede: Only one of them happens while you are away.
translit: Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika min waʿthāʾi-s-safar, wa min kaʾābati-l-munqalab, wa min sūʾi-l-manẓari fi-l-māli wa-l-ahl
trans: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of the journey, from the gloom of the return, and from an ugly sight in property and family.
story: Said with a foot in the stirrup. The first is the road. The second is coming back to nothing worth coming back for. The third is arriving home and finding something wrong there.
note: It opens: O Allah, You are the companion on the journey and the one left in charge of the family.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ وَمِنْ كَآبَةِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ وَمِنْ سُوءِ الْمَنْظَرِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالأَهْلِ
english_full: Malik related to me that he heard that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set foot in the stirrup intending to travel, he would say, "In the name of Allah. O Allah! You are my companion in the journey and the Khalifa of my family. O Allah! Spread out the earth for us and make the journey easy for us. O Allah! I seek refuge with You from the hardship of the journey and from returning to sorrow and a distressing sight regarding property and family

title: Two things promised for one act
lede: Both of them are things people cannot arrange for themselves.
translit: Man sarrahu an yubsaṭa lahu fī rizqihi wa an yunsaʾa lahu fī atharih, fa-l-yaṣil raḥimah
trans: Whoever would like his provision widened and his trace extended, let him keep the ties of his kinship.
story: Athar is the track a person leaves behind them. Both things named are outside anybody's control, and the one action offered in exchange is the phone call nobody wants to make.
arabic: مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَأَنْ يُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "Who ever is pleased that he be granted more wealth and that his lease of life be pro longed, then he should keep good relations with his Kith and kin

title: Who actually counts as maintaining ties
lede: It rules out the obvious case.
translit: Laysa-l-wāṣilu bi-l-mukāfiʾ, wa lākini-l-wāṣilu-lladhī idhā qaṭaʿat raḥimuhu waṣalahā
trans: The one who maintains ties is not the one who repays in kind. The one who maintains ties is the one who, when his relatives cut him off, keeps connecting.
story: Repaying is called something else here. The word is reserved for the case where nothing is coming back.
arabic: لَيْسَ الْوَاصِلُ بِالْمُكَافِئِ، وَلَكِنِ الْوَاصِلُ الَّذِي إِذَا قَطَعَتْ رَحِمُهُ وَصَلَهَا
english_full: Narrated `Abdullah bin `Amr:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Al-Wasil is not the one who recompenses the good done to him by his relatives, but Al-Wasil is the one who keeps good relations with those relatives who had severed the bond of kinship with him

title: What kinship asked for after creation was finished
lede: It was given the thing it asked for immediately.
translit: Qālati-r-raḥim: hādhā maqāmu-l-ʿāʾidhi bika mina-l-qaṭīʿah. Qāla: naʿam, amā tarḍayna an aṣila man waṣalaki wa aqṭaʿa man qaṭaʿaki
trans: Kinship said: this is the place of one seeking refuge in You from being severed. He said: yes. Would you not be content that I keep connection with whoever keeps connection with you, and cut off whoever cuts you off?
story: It said: yes, my Lord. He said: then it is yours. The relationship between a person and their family is described as having its own standing, able to ask for something on its own behalf.
arabic: قَالَتِ الرَّحِمُ هَذَا مَقَامُ الْعَائِذِ بِكَ مِنَ الْقَطِيعَةِ. قَالَ نَعَمْ أَمَا تَرْضَيْنَ أَنْ أَصِلَ مَنْ وَصَلَكِ. وَأَقْطَعَ مَنْ قَطَعَكِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Allah created the creations, and when He finished from His creations, Ar-Rahm i.e., womb said, "(O Allah) at this place I seek refuge with You from all those who sever me (i.e. sever the ties of Kith and kin). Allah said, 'Yes, won't you be pleased that I will keep good relations with the one who will keep good relations with you, and I will sever the relation with the one who will sever the relations with you.' It said, 'Yes, O my Lord.' Allah said, 'Then that is for you ' " Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) added. "Read (in the Qur'an) if you wish, the Statement of Allah: 'Would you then, if you were given the authority, do mischief in the land and sever your ties of kinship?

title: What a woman did with the only thing she was given
lede: Aisha had nothing in the house but one date.
translit: Man yalī min hādhihi-l-banāti shayʾan fa-aḥsana ilayhinna kunna lahu sitran mina-n-nār
trans: Whoever is put in charge of any of these daughters and treats them well, they will be a screen for him from the Fire.
story: A woman came asking, with two daughters. Aisha found nothing but one date and gave it to her. She split it between the two girls, took nothing herself, and left. Aisha told him when he came in, and this is what he said.
arabic: مَنْ يَلِي مِنْ هَذِهِ الْبَنَاتِ شَيْئًا فَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِنَّ كُنَّ لَهُ سِتْرًا مِنَ النَّارِ
english_full: Narrated `Aisha:(the wife of the Prophet) A lady along with her two daughters came to me asking me (for some alms), but she found nothing with me except one date which I gave to her and she divided it between her two daughters, and then she got up and went away. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) came in and I informed him about this story. He said, "Whoever is in charge of (put to test by) these daughters and treats them generously, then they will act as a shield for him from the (Hell) Fire

title: How much of it is down here
lede: The example given is a horse lifting its hoof.
translit: Jaʿala-Llāhu-r-raḥmata miʾata juzʾ, fa-amsaka ʿindahu tisʿatan wa tisʿīna juzʾan, wa anzala fi-l-arḍi juzʾan wāḥidā, fa-min dhālika-l-juzʾi yatarāḥamu-l-khalq
trans: Allah made mercy a hundred parts. He kept ninety nine with Him and sent down one part to the earth. From that one part the creation shows mercy to one another.
story: It ends with the smallest illustration available: a mare lifting her hoof away from her foal in case she catches him. Every kindness anyone has ever received is out of the one part.
arabic: جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الرَّحْمَةَ مِائَةَ جُزْءٍ، فَأَمْسَكَ عِنْدَهُ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ جُزْءًا، وَأَنْزَلَ فِي الأَرْضِ جُزْءًا وَاحِدًا، فَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْجُزْءِ يَتَرَاحَمُ الْخَلْقُ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, Allah divided Mercy into one hundred parts. He kept ninety nine parts with Him and sent down one part to the earth, and because of that, its one single part, His Creations are merciful to each other, so that even the mare lifts up its hoofs away from its baby animal, lest it should trample on it

title: What ordinary work is ranked against
lede: Two comparisons, and both of them are the hardest things on the list.
translit: As-sāʿī ʿalā-l-armalati wa-l-miskīni ka-l-mujāhidi fī sabīli-Llāh, aw ka-lladhī yaṣūmu-n-nahāra wa yaqūmu-l-layl
trans: The one who works to provide for a widow and for the poor is like a man striving in the path of Allah, or like one who fasts the day and stands the night.
story: Sāʿī is the one who goes back and forth, running the errands. It is unglamorous, repetitive work, and it is put level with the two things people admire most.
arabic: السَّاعِي عَلَى الأَرْمَلَةِ وَالْمِسْكِينِ كَالْمُجَاهِدِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، أَوْ كَالَّذِي يَصُومُ النَّهَارَ وَيَقُومُ اللَّيْلَ
english_full: Narrated Safwan bin Salim:The Prophet (ﷺ) said "The one who looks after and works for a widow and for a poor person, is like a warrior fighting for Allah's Cause or like a person who fasts during the day and prays all the night." Narrated Abu Huraira that the Prophet (ﷺ) said as above

title: What the whole thing is compared to
lede: The comparison is not a community. It is an organism.
translit: Tara-l-muʾminīna fī tarāḥumihim wa tawāddihim wa taʿāṭufihim ka-mathali-l-jasad
trans: You see the believers in their mercy to one another, their love for one another and their kindness to one another, like a single body.
story: It continues: when one limb complains, the rest of the body answers it with sleeplessness and fever. Not that the others help. That they cannot sleep.
arabic: تَرَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي تَرَاحُمِهِمْ وَتَوَادِّهِمْ وَتَعَاطُفِهِمْ كَمَثَلِ الْجَسَدِ
english_full: Narrated An-Nu`man bin Bashir:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "You see the believers as regards their being merciful among themselves and showing love among themselves and being kind, resembling one body, so that, if any part of the body is not well then the whole body shares the sleeplessness (insomnia) and fever with it

title: What a planted thing keeps earning
lede: It does not specify who eats.
translit: Mā min muslimin gharasa gharsan fa-akala minhu insānun aw dābbatun illā kāna lahu ṣadaqah
trans: There is no Muslim who plants a plant, and a human being or an animal eats from it, but that it is charity for him.
story: No intention is required at the moment of eating, and the eater does not have to be known or deserving or human. The act was finished years earlier.
arabic: مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ غَرَسَ غَرْسًا فَأَكَلَ مِنْهُ إِنْسَانٌ أَوْ دَابَّةٌ إِلاَّ كَانَ لَهُ صَدَقَةً
english_full: Narrated Anas bin Malik:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If any Muslim plants any plant and a human being or an animal eats of it, he will be rewarded as if he had given that much in charity

title: Three sentences with the same opening
lede: The third one is about saying nothing.
translit: Man kāna yuʾminu bi-Llāhi wa-l-yawmi-l-ākhiri fa-l-yukrim jārah, wa man kāna yuʾminu bi-Llāhi wa-l-yawmi-l-ākhiri fa-l-yukrim ḍayfahu jāʾizatah
trans: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him treat his neighbour well. And whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest with his due.
story: Abu Shurayh asked what the due was. A day and a night, and hospitality is three days, and past that it is charity to him. And the third clause: whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say something good or stay silent.
arabic: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ جَارَهُ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ جَائِزَتَهُ
english_full: Narrated Abu Shuraih Al-Adawi:My ears heard and my eyes saw the Prophet (ﷺ) when he spoke, "Anybody who believes in Allah and the Last Day, should serve his neighbor generously, and anybody who believes in Allah and the Last Day should serve his guest generously by giving him his reward." It was asked. "What is his reward, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" He said, "(To be entertained generously) for a day and a night with high quality of food and the guest has the right to be entertained for three days (with ordinary food) and if he stays longer, what he will be provided with will be regarded as Sadaqa (a charitable gift). And anybody who believes in Allah and the Last Day should talk what is good or keep quiet (i.e. abstain from all kinds of dirty and evil talks)

title: What he said before the man came in, and after
lede: Aisha asked him about the difference.
translit: Biʾsa akhu-l-ʿashīrah, wa biʾsa-bnu-l-ʿashīrah
trans: What an evil brother of his clan, and what an evil son of his clan.
story: He said it seeing the man at the door. When the man sat down he was open and easy with him to his face. Afterwards Aisha asked. He told her the worst of people in station on the Day of Resurrection is the one people abandon out of fear of his foulness.
arabic: بِئْسَ أَخُو الْعَشِيرَةِ، وَبِئْسَ ابْنُ الْعَشِيرَةِ
english_full: Narrated 'Aisha: A man asked permission to enter upon the Prophet. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he said, "What an evil brother of his tribe! And what an evil son of his tribe!" When that man sat down, the Prophet (ﷺ) behaved with him in a nice and polite manner and was completely at ease with him. When that person had left, 'Aisha said (to the Prophet). "O Allah's Apostle! When you saw that man, you said so-and-so about him, then you showed him a kind and polite behavior, and you enjoyed his company?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "O 'Aisha! Have you ever seen me speaking a bad and dirty language? (Remember that) the worst people in Allah's sight on the Day of Resurrection will be those whom the people leave (undisturbed) to be away from their evil (deeds)

title: The announcement that goes out
lede: It moves in one direction and ends on the ground.
translit: Idhā aḥabba-Llāhu ʿabdan nādā Jibrīl: inna-Llāha yuḥibbu fulānan fa-aḥibbah. Fa-yuḥibbuhu Jibrīl, fa-yunādī Jibrīlu fī ahli-s-samāʾ: inna-Llāha yuḥibbu fulānan fa-aḥibbūh
trans: When Allah loves a servant He calls Jibril: Allah loves so and so, so love him. Jibril loves him, and Jibril calls out among the people of the sky: Allah loves so and so, so love him.
story: So the people of the sky love him. Then acceptance is placed for him among the people of the earth. Being liked by people is put at the end of the chain as a consequence rather than the aim.
arabic: إِذَا أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا نَادَى جِبْرِيلَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ فُلاَنًا، فَأَحِبَّهُ. فَيُحِبُّهُ جِبْرِيلُ، فَيُنَادِي جِبْرِيلُ فِي أَهْلِ السَّمَاءِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ فُلاَنًا، فَأَحِبُّوهُ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If Allah loves a person, He calls Gabriel saying: 'Allah loves so and so; O Gabriel, love him.' Gabriel would love him, and then Gabriel would make an announcement among the residents of the Heaven, 'Allah loves so-and-so, therefore, you should love him also.' So, all the residents of the Heavens would love him and then he is granted the pleasure of the people of the earth

title: What happens to an accusation that does not land
lede: Abu Dharr heard him say it.
translit: Lā yarmī rajulun rajulan bi-l-fusūq, wa lā yarmīhi bi-l-kufr, illā-rtaddat ʿalayh
trans: No man throws the charge of wickedness at another, or throws the charge of disbelief at him, without it coming back on him if his companion is not as he said.
story: Nothing is neutral. The accusation either lands or it returns, and there is no third outcome where it simply evaporates.
arabic: لاَ يَرْمِي رَجُلٌ رَجُلاً بِالْفُسُوقِ، وَلاَ يَرْمِيهِ بِالْكُفْرِ، إِلاَّ ارْتَدَّتْ عَلَيْهِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Dhar:That he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying, "If somebody accuses another of Fusuq (by calling him 'Fasiq' i.e. a wicked person) or accuses him of Kufr, such an accusation will revert to him (i.e. the accuser) if his companion (the accused) is innocent

title: What Abu Dharr was still doing decades later
lede: He and his servant were wearing matching cloaks.
translit: Hum ikhwānukum, jaʿalahumu-Llāhu taḥta aydīkum. Fa-man jaʿala-Llāhu akhāhu taḥta yadihi fa-l-yuṭʿimhu mimmā yaʾkul
trans: They are your brothers. Allah placed them under your hand. So whoever has his brother under his hand, let him feed him from what he eats.
story: Someone suggested he take his servant's cloak and make a matching suit of it. He explained: he had once insulted a man about his mother, been told there was still ignorance in him, and had been dressing the man beside him identically ever since.
arabic: هُمْ إِخْوَانُكُمْ، جَعَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ تَحْتَ أَيْدِيكُمْ، فَمَنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ أَخَاهُ تَحْتَ يَدِهِ فَلْيُطْعِمْهُ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ
english_full: Narrated Ma'rur:I saw Abu Dhar wearing a Burd (garment) and his slave too was wearing a Burd, so I said (to Abu Dhar), "If you take this (Burda of your slave) and wear it (along with yours), you will have a nice suit (costume) and you may give him another garment." Abu Dhar said, "There was a quarrel between me and another man whose mother was a non-Arab and I called her bad names. The man mentioned (complained about) me to the Prophet. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Did you abuse so-and-so?" I said, "Yes" He said, "Did you call his mother bad names?" I said, "Yes". He said, "You still have the traits of (the Pre-Islamic period of) ignorance." I said. "(Do I still have ignorance) even now in my old age?" He said, "Yes, they (slaves or servants) are your brothers, and Allah has put them under your command. So the one under whose hand Allah has put his brother, should feed him of what he eats, and give him dresses of what he wears, and should not ask him to do a thing beyond his capacity. And if at all he asks him to do a hard task, he should help him therein

title: Two graves and two small things
lede: He said it, and then did something about it.
translit: Innahumā la-yuʿadhdhabān, wa mā yuʿadhdhabāni fī kabīr. Ammā hādhā fa-kāna lā yastatiru min bawlih, wa ammā hādhā fa-kāna yamshī bi-n-namīmah
trans: They are being punished, and they are not being punished for something major. This one did not keep himself clean of his urine, and this one used to walk about carrying tales.
story: Then he called for a fresh palm branch, split it in two, and planted one on each grave, and said: perhaps it will be lightened for them as long as these do not dry out. In another narration he corrects the phrase: and it is indeed major.
arabic: إِنَّهُمَا لَيُعَذَّبَانِ، وَمَا يُعَذَّبَانِ فِي كَبِيرٍ، أَمَّا هَذَا فَكَانَ لاَ يَسْتَتِرُ مِنْ بَوْلِهِ، وَأَمَّا هَذَا فَكَانَ يَمْشِي بِالنَّمِيمَةِ
english_full: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) passed by two graves and said, "Both of them (persons in the grave) are being tortured, and they are not being tortured for a major sin. This one used not to save himself from being soiled with his urine, and the other used to go about with calumnies (among the people to rouse hostilities, e.g., one goes to a person and tells him that so-and-so says about him such-and-such evil things). The Prophet (ﷺ) then asked for a green leaf of a date-palm tree, split it into two pieces and planted one on each grave and said, "It is hoped that their punishment may be abated till those two pieces of the leaf get dried." (See Hadith No 215, Vol)

title: What fasting is worth without the rest
lede: It names three things and then dismisses the fast.
translit: Man lam yadaʿ qawla-z-zūri wa-l-ʿamala bihi wa-l-jahl, fa-laysa lillāhi ḥājatun an yadaʿa ṭaʿāmahu wa sharābah
trans: Whoever does not give up false speech and acting on it, and ignorance, Allah has no need of his giving up his food and his drink.
arabic: مَنْ لَمْ يَدَعْ قَوْلَ الزُّورِ وَالْعَمَلَ بِهِ وَالْجَهْلَ فَلَيْسَ لِلَّهِ حَاجَةٌ أَنْ يَدَعَ طَعَامَهُ وَشَرَابَهُ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever does not give up false statements (i.e. telling lies), and evil deeds, and speaking bad words to others, Allah is not in need of his (fasting) leaving his food and drink

title: Who is worst in the sight of Allah
lede: It is defined by what they do with their face.
translit: Tajidu min sharri-n-nāsi yawma-l-qiyāmati ʿinda-Llāhi dha-l-wajhayn, alladhī yaʾtī hāʾulāʾi bi-wajh
trans: You will find among the worst of people with Allah on the Day of Resurrection the one with two faces, who comes to these with one face,
story: And to those with another. It is not lying and it is not gossip. It is being a different person depending on which room you are standing in.
arabic: تَجِدُ مِنْ شَرِّ النَّاسِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ ذَا الْوَجْهَيْنِ، الَّذِي يَأْتِي هَؤُلاَءِ بِوَجْهٍ
english_full: Narrated Abu Huraira:The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The worst people in the Sight of Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be the double faced people who appear to some people with one face and to other people with another face

title: What he said to a man praising someone
lede: He repeated it several times.
translit: Wayḥaka qaṭaʿta ʿunuqa ṣāḥibik. In kāna aḥadukum mādiḥan lā maḥālata fa-l-yaqul: aḥsibu kadhā wa kadhā
trans: Woe to you, you have cut your companion's neck. If one of you must praise, let him say: I think such and such.
story: A man had been mentioned and someone praised him well. He gave the wording to use instead, and the reason: if he really believes it to be so, and his reckoner is Allah, and let no one declare anyone pure before Allah.
arabic: وَيْحَكَ قَطَعْتَ عُنُقَ صَاحِبِكَ ـ يَقُولُهُ مِرَارًا ـ إِنْ كَانَ أَحَدُكُمْ مَادِحًا لاَ مَحَالَةَ فَلْيَقُلْ أَحْسِبُ كَذَا وَكَذَا
english_full: Narrated Abu Bakra:A man was mentioned before the Prophet (ﷺ) and another man praised him greatly The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "May Allah's Mercy be on you ! You have cut the neck of your friend." The Prophet (ﷺ) repeated this sentence many times and said, "If it is indispensable for anyone of you to praise someone, then he should say, 'I think that he is so-and-so," if he really thinks that he is such. Allah is the One Who will take his accounts (as He knows his reality) and no-one can sanctify anybody before Allah." (Khalid said, "Woe to you," instead of "Allah's Mercy be on you)

title: Four instructions in a row, all of them negative
lede: Then one that is not.
translit: Lā tabāghaḍū, wa lā taḥāsadū, wa lā tadābarū, wa kūnū ʿibāda-Llāhi ikhwānā. Wa lā yaḥillu li-muslimin an yahjura akhāhu fawqa thalāthati ayyām
trans: Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another. Be servants of Allah, brothers. And it is not lawful for a Muslim to cut off his brother beyond three days.
story: Tadābur is standing back to back, the posture of two people who have decided not to see each other. It is named alongside hatred and envy as though it were the same size of thing.
arabic: لاَ تَبَاغَضُوا، وَلاَ تَحَاسَدُوا، وَلاَ تَدَابَرُوا، وَكُونُوا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ إِخْوَانًا، وَلاَ يَحِلُّ لِمُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَهْجُرَ أَخَاهُ فَوْقَ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ
english_full: Narrated Anas bin Malik:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Do not hate one another, and do not be jealous of one another, and do not desert each other, and O, Allah's worshipers! Be brothers. Lo! It is not permissible for any Muslim to desert (not talk to) his brother (Muslim) for more than three days

title: The sin he changed position to say twice
lede: He had been reclining until then.
translit: Alā wa qawlu-z-zūri wa shahādatu-z-zūr
trans: Beware of false speech and false testimony. Beware of false speech and false testimony.
story: He asked whether he should tell them the greatest of the major sins. They said yes. He named associating others with Allah, and being undutiful to parents. He had been leaning back. Then he sat up and said this, and Abu Bakrah says he kept repeating it until they wished he would stop.
arabic: أَلاَ وَقَوْلُ الزُّورِ وَشَهَادَةُ الزُّورِ، أَلاَ وَقَوْلُ الزُّورِ وَشَهَادَةُ الزُّورِ
english_full: Narrated Abu Bakra:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said thrice, "Shall I not inform you of the biggest of the great sins?" We said, "Yes, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)" He said, "To join partners in worship with Allah: to be undutiful to one's parents." The Prophet (ﷺ) sat up after he had been reclining and added, "And I warn you against giving forged statement and a false witness; I warn you against giving a forged statement and a false witness." The Prophet kept on saying that warning till we thought that he would not stop

title: What he told a man who wanted one answer
lede: The people around thought he was being rude.
translit: Taʿbudu-Llāha lā tushriku bihi shayʾā, wa tuqīmu-ṣ-ṣalāh, wa tuʾti-z-zakāh, wa taṣilu-r-raḥim
trans: You worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, you establish the prayer, you give the zakat, and you keep the ties of kinship.
story: A man said: tell me a deed that will put me in the Garden. The people said: what is wrong with him. He said: leave him, he has a need. Then he gave four things, and the fourth is the one that involves other people.
arabic: تَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ لاَ تُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا، وَتُقِيمُ الصَّلاَةَ، وَتُؤْتِي الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصِلُ الرَّحِمَ
english_full: Narrated Abu Aiyub Al-Ansari:A man said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Inform me of a deed which will make me enter Paradise." The people said, "What is the matter with him? What is the matter with him?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "He has something to ask (what he needs greatly)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to him), (In order to enter Paradise) you should worship Allah and join none in worship with Him: You should offer prayers perfectly, give obligatory charity (Zakat), and keep good relations with your Kith and kin." He then said, "Leave it!" (The sub-narrator said, "It seems that the Prophet (ﷺ) was riding his she camel

title: What he told the young men after twenty nights
lede: He worked out that they were homesick before they said so.
translit: Irjiʿū ilā ahlīkum fa-ʿallimūhum wa murūhum, wa ṣallū kamā raʾaytumūnī uṣallī
trans: Go back to your families, and teach them and instruct them, and pray as you have seen me pray.
